articles.title: "A sign of weakness....": Former NFL quarterback delivers powerful mental health message to young football players
articles.summary: Football teaches young athletes to fight through pain, handle pressure and keep pushing when the odds are against them. But former NFL quarterback B.J.
articles.body: Football teaches young athletes to fight through pain, handle pressure and keep pushing when the odds are against them. But former NFL quarterback B.J. Daniels wants student-athletes to understand that strength also means knowing when to ask for help. At a youth behavioral health summit in Florida, Daniels shared his own experiences with personal struggles and encouraged young players to speak openly about their mental health. His message was simple but powerful: athletes do not have to hide their emotions to prove their toughness.B.J. Daniels opens up about mental health struggles among athletesDaniels met with football players from six Pinellas County high schools at the second annual Mind Shift Youth Behavioral Health Summit on October 9. Organised in partnership with Evara Health, Pinellas County Schools and the Juvenile Welfare Board, the event focused on helping young athletes manage stress, build resilience and understand that their worth extends beyond their performance.The former University of South Florida standout, who won a Super Bowl during his professional career, spoke about the challenges he faced both on and off the field.“I face so many different challenges,” said Daniels, per WFLA. “Some were seen, some were unseen, and some I was scared to talk about.”His words offered a reminder that even experienced athletes can face struggles that others never notice. For young players who feel pressure to appear confident and strong, opening up about difficult emotions can seem daunting.Daniels urged the students to find people they trust rather than face those challenges alone.“I want these young men to know that it’s okay to not be okay and find ways to communicate and know that there’s a locker room that I would call your community that’s around you that will always support you,” he added.The summit also highlighted the importance of creating safe spaces where young people can discuss their feelings without fear of judgment. Organisers cited data showing that one in five young people in Pinellas County will experience a mental health condition during their lifetime.B.J. Daniels encourages young athletes to ask for helpDaniels continued the conversation on Instagram, sharing photographs from the summit and explaining why athletes should feel comfortable seeking support.“Athletes can feel like they have to be tough all the time — like admitting that something is bothering you is a sign of weakness,” he wrote in the caption. “But asking for help doesn’t make you less of an athlete. It gives you the confidence to face difficult things, take care of yourself, and be there for the people counting on you.”The message also resonated with the students who attended the event. Clearwater High School linebacker Jayeon Jackson spoke about seeing former teammates make poor decisions, while senior Jekobi Brown highlighted the value of positive self-talk.“I’ve learned that talking to yourself isn’t a bad thing to do,” Brown said. “Talking to yourself could get you out of terrible decisions, and it could change your life.”Jackson also offered an encouraging message: “Keep speaking positively to yourself and never give up on your dreams,” he added.Through his work with Evara Health, where he serves as manager of strategic growth and partnerships, Daniels is helping bring mental health conversations into spaces where young athletes may otherwise feel reluctant to speak. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment in Six Flags draws attention as investigators examine Goliath’s safety record
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags has taken on a different significance as a fatal roller coaster accident at Six Flags Over Georgia draws attention
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags has taken on a different significance as a fatal roller coaster accident at Six Flags Over Georgia draws attention to ride safety. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end is an ambassador and investor in the amusement park company, making the developing investigation an important story for readers following his business interests beyond football. On October 12, 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died after being ejected from the Goliath roller coaster. Four other riders, all minors, suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Authorities are still working to establish exactly what happened.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment meets renewed scrutinyKelce has built a public profile that extends beyond his NFL career, with business interests and brand partnerships adding to his growing commercial presence. His role as a Six Flags ambassador and investor connects him to one of the best-known names in the amusement park industry.However, the fatal incident at the Georgia park raises serious questions about ride safety and operational oversight. It is important to distinguish Kelce’s business association from the investigation itself. There is no information in the available reporting that links the NFL star to the operation, maintenance or safety decisions involving Goliath.Six Flags Over Georgia reopened on October 16 for its Fright Fest event, but Goliath remains closed. Park officials have not announced a date for the roller coaster’s return, and the attraction cannot resume operation until state investigators complete the required review.The accident also places greater attention on how amusement parks maintain public confidence when a serious incident occurs. For a company with a broad entertainment business, safety assurances must rest on verified findings, transparent communication and effective oversight.Six Flags Goliath investigation raises questions about ride safetyInvestigators are examining the circumstances surrounding Kariem’s death, including the ride’s operation and its restraint system. Cobb County police said preliminary witness and employee interviews indicated that Kariem was ejected, struck other riders and fell beneath the attraction.Several eyewitness accounts have raised further questions. Erica Billups told The Associated Press that her children encountered a restraint that repeatedly became unlocked about an hour before the fatal incident. Her account has not been independently verified by investigators, and officials have not established a connection between that reported problem and the death.State inspection records have also attracted attention. According to WSB-TV, records from Goliath’s March 16, 2026, inspection noted bushings that needed replacement. However, the state inspection reportedly recorded no violations, deficiencies, citations or red tags. The available records do not establish whether those components had any connection to the accident.Georgia authorities are reviewing evidence, interviewing witnesses and examining relevant records. The coaster’s manufacturer, Bolliger & Mabillard, is also investigating.For Kelce and Six Flags, the immediate issue is not speculation about responsibility but the need for a clear account of what happened. Until investigators establish the cause, questions about the restraint system, maintenance and ride procedures remain unanswered. articles.body: Kansas City’s sports future is taking shape around ambitious stadium plans, public spending decisions and questions about who should pay for professional sports facilities. Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the ownership group of the Kansas City Current, have a stake in the city’s wider sporting landscape. As officials consider public funding for a new Kansas City Royals stadium, concerns are growing over competing budget priorities and the future of the Truman Sports Complex. The debate highlights a difficult question for Kansas City: how can it support major sports investments while protecting essential public services?Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ KC Current ownership amid stadium debatePatrick and Brittany Mahomes have expanded their connection to Kansas City beyond football through their ownership stake in the KC Current, the city’s professional women’s soccer team. Their involvement reflects the growing appeal of sports investments and the role local franchises can play in shaping a city’s identity.However, Kansas City’s latest stadium debate focuses on the financial choices facing local officials rather than the Current itself. According to Field of Schemes, the Kansas City Council approved a plan to use sales tax revenue for a proposed Royals stadium. The decision has raised concerns that money normally reserved for public safety could become less available for projects such as a new jail and police body cameras.Councilmember Johnathan Duncan, one of two members who opposed the measure, said, “For us to divert those revenues to pay for a for-profit business,” and added, “is a concern. And I wish it were more of a concern to the mayor and my colleagues.”The funding question matters because stadium deals can affect public budgets long after construction begins. Residents must weigh the potential economic benefits of a new venue against the cost of providing essential services.Kansas City stadium plans raise questions about the Truman Sports ComplexThe discussion extends beyond the Royals’ proposed new home. With the Royals and Kansas City Chiefs reportedly heading towards new stadium arrangements, a task force has presented redevelopment concepts for the Truman Sports Complex, where the teams have played for decades.The ideas include a smaller stadium inspired by Arrowhead, walking trails and other entertainment features. Yet the proposal has prompted questions about its cost, funding and long-term demand.Jackson County Executive Phil LeVota warned about the consequences of leaving the site unused, saying, “if we don’t do something with that area, it will stay in disrepair and it will be a blight,”The challenge is to create a viable future for the land without placing an unreasonable burden on taxpayers. Attractive renderings alone cannot guarantee investment, visitors or lasting economic growth.For Mahomes and Brittany, their KC Current ownership provides a separate link to Kansas City’s sports community. articles.title: 49ers' Brock Purdy Makes NFL History Breaking Lamar Jackson's Passing Record
articles.summary: Brock Purdy's hyper-efficient start to his NFL career has earned him a spot in the history books on Monday.
articles.body:
Brock Purdy's hyper-efficient start to his NFL career has earned him a spot in the history books on Monday.

The San Francisco 49ers quarterback has now surpassed 1,500 pass attempts in his career, meaning he now qualifies for a handful of all-time rankings. He's now No. 1 all time in passer rating (105.4), adjusted yards per attempt (8.7) and adjusted net yards per attempt (7.9), among other statistics.

Lamar Jackson previously held the passer rating record at 102.7, but it now belongs to Purdy. Some other notable quarterbacks just below him include Aaron Rodgers, Joe Burrow, Patrick Mahomes, Russell Wilson, Drew Brees, Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.

It's fair to say that most didn't expect Purdy to have this kind of career when he was drafted with the 262nd overall pick in 2022, but he's quickly established himself as one of the best quarterbacks in the league year in and year out.

He had an MVP-caliber campaign in just his second NFL season and led the Niners to a Super Bowl appearance that year. This year, he has San Francisco off to a 5-0 start, and the 49ers appear capable of winning it all.

Of course, Purdy has had plenty of help along the way, from coordinators and coaches to talented players like George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey, but his stats are a testament to how well he's played over his first few years.

Purdy, still just 26, could end up being one of the best quarterbacks of his generation, but he's still chasing his first Super Bowl, an MVP and other accolades.

For now, he remains one of the most effecient quarterbacks the league has ever seen.

articles.title: NFL Network's Michael Robinson Apologizes to Jalen Hurts, Eagles After Comments on Blood Clots
articles.summary: After making speculative comments on Jalen Hurts' blood clots, NFL Network's Michael Robinson has issued an apology to the quarterback and the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
After making speculative comments on Jalen Hurts' blood clots, NFL Network's Michael Robinson has issued an apology to the quarterback and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Robinson called his comments "unfounded" and said he shouldn't have "speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to his team."

After Hurts was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers, Robinson said the Eagles could be "incentivized to go into the draft and maybe look for a quarterback" and were using Hurts' injury as an excuse to move away from him.

Robinson also suggested that Hurts wanted to get himself "out of the fray" amid a rocky start to the season for the Eagles.

"It looked like they were trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts just so that they could have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts," Robinson said on NFL Gameday Kickoff . "And, again, I'm not saying I know nothing, guys. But if I'm just playing devil's advocate here, and I'm thinking that way, if I'm Jalen Hurts — or anybody in Jalen Hurts' camp — I'm saying, 'Well if everybody's hurt, I'm hurt, too.' To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season … he's pulling himself out so that this doesn't look like it's on me."

Hurts was placed on the injured reserve on Saturday because of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. He was ruled out for the season on Monday after doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts struggled to start the season, throwing for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions, along with 107 rushing yards and a score on the ground through his first five games.

The Eagles are 2-4 to start the year, and things will only get more difficult without their starting quarterback.

articles.title: “Spend an hour of your time and give something”: How Tom Brady's high school habit inspired a blood donation drive that drew 20,000 donors and could save 60,000 lives
articles.summary: Tom Brady has spent years chasing records on the football field.
articles.body: Tom Brady has spent years chasing records on the football field. But one habit he picked up long before his NFL career has nothing to do with touchdowns or Super Bowl rings. Brady has donated blood since high school. In Sept. 2024, he used that experience to encourage college football fans to do the same, joining a campaign that brought rival schools together for a cause bigger than the game.The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback teamed up with Abbott and the Big Ten Conference for the We Give Blood Drive. The campaign ran during the 2024 college football season and ended with nearly 20,000 people donating blood. Tom Brady reveals the high school habit behind his blood donation campaignBrady shared the personal story in an interview with Axios. TB12 explained that blood donation had been part of his life since his school days.“I've been giving blood since I was in high school,” Brady told Axios.One statistic particularly caught his attention. “The one stat that stood out to me was every person that donates saves up to three lives,” he said in the same interview.Brady also made the process sound straightforward. “You just go there and spend an hour of your time and give something that can really help a lot of people in need,” he told Axios.That was the point he wanted fans to take away. People do not need to be professional athletes or wealthy donors to help someone. Giving blood is a practical way to support patients who need transfusions after accidents, during cancer treatment or following childbirth complications.Brady's involvement also came as the United States faced a serious blood shortage. On September 26, 2024, the American Red Cross reported an emergency shortage after donations dropped during the summer. The campaign aimed to bring more people, especially younger donors, into the process.How Tom Brady's Big Ten blood drive raised $1 million for community healthAbbott and the Big Ten launched the We Give Blood Drive on September 26, 2024. The competition involved all 18 Big Ten universities, with students, alumni and fans donating blood in support of their chosen school.Each donation earned a point on the leaderboard. Abbott promised $1 million to the university that collected the most donations, with the money earmarked for student or community health projects.It gave college football fans another reason to back their school. Instead of cheering only for a win on Saturday, they could help their university climb the standings by donating blood.The competition ran through December 6, 2024, and Abbott announced the winner on December 7 at the Discover Big Ten Football Championship Game in Indianapolis.The University of Nebraska-Lincoln finished first and received the $1 million grant. Abbott reported that nearly 20,000 students, alumni and fans had donated blood during the campaign, potentially helping save as many as 60,000 lives.There was another encouraging result. Abbott said more than half of the donors at campus blood drives gave blood for the first time. That meant the campaign reached people who might not otherwise have considered donating.Brady did not need a football record to make his point. He brought attention to a habit he had kept since high school and helped connect it with a nationwide effort. The final numbers belonged to the thousands who showed up to donate, but his message was simple: an hour of your time could help someone who needs it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A week after mismanaging end of overtime, Commanders coach and QB seemed confused about a key 4th down try
articles.summary: For a second straight week, Dan Quinn and Jayden Daniels seemed lost during a key situation.
articles.body:
Last week, the Washington Commanders completely screwed up an end-of-game scenario and let time run out in overtime without getting a field goal attempt off .

On Monday night, the Commanders appeared to have another gaffe in a game that got tight in the second half before the 49ers won, 23-17 . While it wasn't quite as bad as last week, it was an embarrassment. It might also force Commanders owners to examine what's happening with their team, especially with head coach Dan Quinn.

The Commanders went for it on fourth-and-2 at the San Francisco 13-yard line in the second quarter. That was reasonable, considering the situation. The Commanders trailed 13-3 against the 49ers at the time. But then quarterback Jayden Daniels inexplicably threw the ball away even though it was fourth down. There was a flag down and perhaps he thought it was on the 49ers, but even if that was the case then it was a free play. The penalty ended up being an illegal shift on the Commanders, another mental error in a key spot.

No matter the reason for Daniels throwing the ball away when there was no real downside to forcing it into a receiver, it was another startling lack of awareness from him. Daniels was at the center of the issues against the Giants in overtime last week, when he let time run down while in the huddle and then got tackled, which allowed the clock to run out.

Daniels' throwing it away was bad, and then it got even weirder.

ESPN showed Quinn on the sideline, apparently calling for a field goal, then having a surprised reaction when it looked like he was told that the previous play was fourth down. The ESPN halftime show addressed Quinn seemingly not knowing it was fourth down on the play in which Daniels strangely threw it away.

After the game, Quinn said he was aware it was fourth down but wasn't clear if the penalty would give them a chance at a field goal try.

"I definitely knew it was fourth down. We were going for it," Quinn said. "I think what you were referring to, I was probably saying like, 'with the illegal shift there's not a penalty to go for a field goal.' It's the turn on downs. Like, I think somebody asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?' So, now we were going for it."

Quinn doesn't call offensive or defensive plays for the Commanders. Managing the game is his most important job on the sideline, and for the second straight week the Commanders inexcusably had very little awareness of the situation in a key spot.

Quinn was likely already on the hot seat after a poor 2025 season and a 1-4-1 start to this season. This could make his seat even hotter.

articles.title: Mike Evans Injured, Latest Updates on 49ers Star's Achilles After Exiting MNF vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers controlled the early going of Monday's game against the Washington Commanders, but it wasn't all good news for the NFC West team.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers controlled the early going of Monday's game against the Washington Commanders, but it wasn't all good news for the NFC West team.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported wide receiver Mike Evans was ruled out for the remainder of the contest with an Achilles injury. He limped to the locker room shortly before halftime and was ruled out following intermission.

After the game, head coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed the injury:

Evans had an injury designation of Achilles and ribs coming into the game, but the 49ers announced he was active prior to kickoff.

The veteran was having an excellent game prior to the setback with three catches for 94 yards, 54 of which came on a single reception. It was more of the same after he dominated his last game against the Seattle Seahawks with seven catches for 113 yards and one touchdown.

Evans arrived in San Francisco this offseason after establishing himself as a franchise legend for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The No. 7 overall pick of the 2014 NFL draft surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first 11 years in the league. He was also a six-time Pro Bowler during that span and is one of the best players in Tampa Bay history.

However, injuries limited him to just eight games last season, which snapped his streak.

Evans' health is now under the microscope again following Monday's setback.

Wide receiver was already a position of concern for the 49ers even before this injury, as Deebo Samuel was sidelined against the Commanders. Ricky Pearsall is also out for the season, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are sidelined as well.

While the team can rely on running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle, it will be up to players such as Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing to produce if Evans is out for an extended amount of time.

articles.title: “Hopefully do it with an organization that legitimately impacts and helps people”: How Brock Purdy turned My Cause My Cleats into a way to help children and disaster victims
articles.summary: Brock Purdy has used the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign to support two very different causes.
articles.body: Brock Purdy has used the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign to support two very different causes. In 2023, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback highlighted an organization that helps children in foster care. A year later, he chose Samaritan's Purse after Hurricane Helene devastated parts of the United States. Purdy's choices also came with a clear goal: use his NFL profile to bring attention and money to people who need help.Brock Purdy backed children in foster care with his 2023 cleatsOn Nov. 30, 2023, Child Advocates of Silicon Valley announced that Purdy had selected the nonprofit for the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign. He wore custom cleats featuring its logo during the 49ers' December 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.The organization supports children who have experienced abuse, neglect or abandonment and entered the Santa Clara County dependency court system. It recruits and trains Court Appointed Special Advocate volunteers, who help make sure children receive support as they navigate the system.Purdy's selection gave the organization a chance to reach NFL fans who might not have known about its work. Child Advocates also launched a fundraising drive called the "13 for 13 Challenge," asking supporters to donate $13, matching Purdy's jersey number. Northern California Toyota dealers offered to match donations up to $10,000.The effort gained traction as Purdy enjoyed a strong season with San Francisco. Per reports, Purdy had raised more than $4,400 at that point and led the campaign's Visa Challenge.Child Advocates CEO Frederick J. Ferrer praised the quarterback's decision in the nonprofit's November 30 announcement."For Brock Purdy to include children in foster care and raise awareness about the work that we do, is absolutely remarkable," Ferrer said.The campaign was about more than a pair of custom shoes. Purdy helped put a spotlight on children who often receive less public attention than high-profile causes. Hurricane Helene influenced Brock Purdy's 2024 charity choicePurdy picked Samaritan's Purse for the 2024 edition of My Cause My Cleats. The Christian humanitarian organization provides emergency assistance to communities affected by disasters and other crises.Hurricane Helene had struck the southeastern United States in late September 2024, causing widespread damage and flooding. Purdy wanted to support an organization already working on the ground.Speaking at a 49ers press conference on December 6, 2024, Purdy explained his decision."I was just thinking about if I'm going to have a chance to raise money, I'd like to hopefully do it with an organization that legitimately impacts and helps people in need," he said.He then explained why the hurricane influenced his choice. "Samaritan's Purse has done that and they are doing that," Purdy said, referring to its relief work.He added that he hoped the campaign could raise money to help people affected by the hurricane.Purdy's signed custom cleats appeared on the official NFL Auction website, with the listing identifying Samaritan's Purse as the beneficiary. The NFL Foundation allocates proceeds from My Cause My Cleats auctions to the charities selected by participating players.The available records do not establish the final amount raised from Purdy's 2024 cleats, so it would be inaccurate to attach a specific donation figure to the campaign.Still, the quarterback's choices tell a clear story. In 2023, he helped raise awareness for children in foster care close to the 49ers' home. In 2024, he turned to disaster relief after a devastating hurricane. Both campaigns gave him a way to support people outside football without claiming credit for money he did not personally donate.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. "I didn't grow up seeing my family get taken advantage of. My biggest fear in life is letting the wrong people into my son's inner circle and losing everything I've worked for. I genuinely wish more athletes had someone in their corner keeping it 100% real with them."Her comments offer a glimpse into a side of professional football that rarely appears in game coverage. A player's success can bring wealth, attention and new relationships, but it can also make it harder to judge who genuinely cares about him. She has made it clear that protecting his financial future is among her priorities, particularly as he navigates life in the public eye."It would help so many young guys protect their future from the women of nowadays. Protecting my son from women trying to target his fortune and take his millions is a top priority for me. Seeing your child get taken advantage of should be every parent's biggest fear. I'm a mom that protects my son."Her remarks reflect a protective approach to parenting, although they also express a broad concern about the people who may approach wealthy athletes for financial reasons. articles.body: Kristin Juszczyk and Claire Kittle are giving San Francisco 49ers fans a closer look at the lives behind the team's biggest names. The longtime friends, married to fullback Kyle Juszczyk and tight end George Kittle, are sharing their experiences through their YouTube series, Wife'd Up, Mic'd Up. During an appearance on ABC's Good Morning America on Monday, October 19, they discussed the project and what it means to tell their own stories. From game-day routines to emotional moments in the stands, the series covers a side of NFL life that rarely makes the broadcast.Kristin Juszczyk and Claire Kittle take fans beyond the 49ers sidelinesNFL coverage tends to follow players from warm-ups through the final whistle. Kristin and Claire's series looks at what happens around those moments, including travel, preparations, time with friends and the nerves that come with watching a loved one play a physically demanding sport.Their connection is a big part of the appeal. They have spent years dealing with the same schedule, sharing the excitement of wins and coping with the uncertainty that comes with an NFL season. Their show draws on that familiarity rather than trying to create drama for the cameras.Still, life around football is not always fun and games. One episode captured Claire reacting emotionally when George suffered an injury. The moment showed the personal cost of watching a partner get hurt, something a live broadcast can rarely explore beyond the medical update and replay.There is plenty of humor, too. Kristin once joked about what happens when Claire gets carried away after a 49ers win."When Claire gets happy, I get abused. She has cute aggression with me," Kristin said.The exchange offers a glimpse of their friendship away from the football field. articles.title: 49ers Beat Commanders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jayden Daniels, Purdy, CMC, Top Players
articles.summary: Led by a standout performance from Brock Purdy, the San Francisco 49ers held off a late comeback attempt from Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders for a 23-17 victory at home.
articles.body:
Led by a standout performance from Brock Purdy, the San Francisco 49ers held off a late comeback attempt from Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders for a 23-17 victory at home.

Ahead of the game, the undefeated 49ers were 7.5-point favorites over the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

With the win, San Francisco remained one of three undefeated teams in the NFL and became the first to reach six wins.

San Francisco led 20-3 at halftime before Washington mounted a fourth-quarter rally. The 49ers were outscored 14-3 in the second half, but a sack on Daniels during the Commanders' final possession sealed their 23-17 victory.

The 49ers came out firing, scoring two touchdowns in the first quarter.

Purdy connected with tight end George Kittle on an 11-yard pass before Christian McCaffrey capped a 72-yard drive with a rushing touchdown to give San Francisco a 13-3 lead after one quarter.

The Commanders' offense struggled to move the ball in the first half, managing just one field goal before a series of punts and a turnover on downs. The turnover came after Daniels scrambled on fourth-and-2 before throwing the ball out of bounds , seemingly to avoid a sack.

"You don't throw (the) ball away on fourth down," ESPN analyst Troy Aikman said. "You gotta at least give your receiver an opportunity."

Despite a McCaffrey fumble in the second quarter, the 49ers entered halftime with a commanding 20-3 lead as the running back made up for his blunder with his second touchdown of the game.

Washington slowed the 49ers in the second half, holding them to a field goal while finding the end zone for the first time on a short pass from Daniels to Stefon Diggs. The touchdown cut San Francisco's lead to 23-10 heading into the fourth quarter.

Two forced three-and-outs by the Commanders' defense and a touchdown reception by Rachaad White off a pass from Daniels cut the 49ers' lead to one score.

The Commanders ate up the clock on a 5:52 drive but turned the ball over on downs at San Francisco's 27-yard line after an incomplete pass to Treylon Burks in the end zone on fourth-and-3.

Washington's defense forced a three-and-out, giving the offense the ball back with 52 seconds left and a chance to take the lead. However, the 49ers' defense stood strong, sacking Daniels on the final play to seal the victory.

The 49ers will hit the road Sunday to face the Atlanta Falcons at 1 p.m. ET, while the Commanders head into their bye week.

articles.summary: San Francisco sigue en la cima de la división Oeste de la Conferencia Nacional (NFC) con una marca de 6-0
articles.body: Los San Francisco 49ers derrotaron por 17-23 a los Washington Commanders para mantenerse invictos en el partido con el que cerró la semana seis de la temporada de la NFL. Brock Purdy lideró a los 49ers con 264 yardas por pase y un envío a las diagonales. Christian McCaffrey colaboró con dos anotaciones por acarreo. Con Washington, Jayden Daniels pasó para 300 yardas y dos envíos de 'touchdown'. San Francisco sigue en la cima de la división Oeste de la Conferencia Nacional (NFC) con marca de 6-0. Commanders es último en la división Este de la NFC con récord de un ganado, cuatro derrotas y un empate. Los 49ers mostraron su jerarquía en la primera mitad. En su serie inaugural llevaron el balón a través de 64 yardas en nueve jugadas en una ofensiva que coronaron con un envío de Brock Purdy a las diagonales que atrapó George Kittle para tomar ventaja de 0-7. Luego de un gol de campo de 51 yardas que hizo bueno Drew Stevens, que colocó el marcador 3-7, los gambusinos respondieron con otra larga ofensiva que recorrió 72 yardas en ocho jugadas hasta la anotación por la vía terrestre de Christian McCaffrey, que los colocó 3-13, por el punto extra fallado de Eddy Piñeiro. En el segundo cuarto la defensiva de Commanders detuvo al ataque local cuando K'Lavon Chaisson provocó un balón suelto sobre McCaffrey, acierto que su ofensiva no capitalizó. San Francisco volvió a la carga con otra largo recorrido de 69 yardas en 14 jugadas que concluyó con el segundo acarreo a la zona pintada de Christian McCaffrey que mandó el partido al descanso 3-20. El equipo de Kyle Shanahan mantuvo su dominio en el reloj en el tercer cuarto, el cual arrancó con un ataque de 11 jugadas en las que recorrió 65 yardas en poco más de seis minutos, que concluyó con un gol de campo de 33 yardas que conectó Piñeiro para ponerse 3-23. Washington reaccionó al final del periodo. Jayden Daniels al fin estableció su ataque con una serie de 65 yardas de 11 jugadas que coronó con un envío de anotación para Stefon Diggs que los acercó 10-23. Reacción que continuó en el último cuarto con una ofensiva que concluyó con otro envío a la zona pintada que atrapó Rachaad White que recortó a 17-23. Ante el apagón que sufrió el ataque de los gambusinos en la segunda mitad, Washington tuvo una última serie para intentar dar la vuelta al marcador, pero la defensiva detuvo a Daniels para sellar la victoria y conservar el invicto.

articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 7: Are the 2-4 Rams even a playoff team after a miserable start?
articles.summary: A team that looked like one of the strongest Super Bowl favorites in recent years has to worry about simply sneaking into the playoffs as a wild-card team.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

It's six weeks into the season and the Los Angeles Rams are already up against history, in terms of making a Super Bowl.

No NFL team has started a season 2-4 and made a Super Bowl, much less win it. But at this point, discussing the Rams and the Super Bowl seems foolish. Forget all the offseason hype. The games started and the Rams haven't looked anywhere near a championship contender. They beat a Giants team that lost quarterback Jaxson Dart in the first quarter and then needed two touchdowns in the final four minutes to beat an Eagles team that is 2-4. Still, 3-3 would have been OK.

Then the Rams lost at home to a Cardinals team that was 1-4 and didn't even score a touchdown, setting off the alarms that the Rams might not even be a playoff team this season. The Rams have a big hole to dig out of and the path got tougher after Sean McVay's injury report on Monday. Receiver Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and will miss six to 10 weeks, according to McVay. Receiver depth behind Puka Nacua and Adams was a major concern going into the season, and now the Rams might have to play most of the rest of their season without one of their two reliable receivers.

That wasn't all. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner will miss multiple weeks with a groin injury and kicker Blake Grupe, just signed last week, went on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury . The Rams' kicking situation has been a mess and the revolving door continues.

It hasn't been the only mess. If there is good news for the Rams, it's that their remaining schedule is the seventh-easiest in the NFL, according to Tankathon. That gives the Rams a shot to rally and make the playoffs.

In five seasons since the NFL started using a 17-game schedule, only four of 30 wild-card teams have been 9-8 (three others were 9-7-1). Realistically, the Rams need to get to 10 wins to have a shot at the playoffs. That means an 8-3 finish, at worst. They still have a game left at San Francisco, two against Seattle and one against the 5-0 Chiefs, among others. And the Rams couldn't even beat the Cardinals in Week 6, so no game can be counted on as an easy win.

"We won't win a game unless we figure out how not to beat ourselves," McVay said after Sunday's game .

The Rams looked like they might be dominant coming into the season. Even after a few losses, the situation didn't seem dire. After the defeat to the Cardinals, and more key injuries, the Rams might be reaching a point of no return. Amazingly, a team that looked like one of the strongest Super Bowl favorites in recent years has to worry about simply sneaking into the playoffs as a wild-card team.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 6 of the NFL season:

Nobody in the Dolphins' organization would admit it publicly, but they have to be keeping an eye on the race for the first overall draft pick. The Titans seemed like they would give the Dolphins the biggest run for the top selection. (More on the Chargers, the NFL's lone 0-6 team right after this take on the Dolphins.) Everyone in Miami should have been happy to see Tennessee get its first win Sunday over Indianapolis. Yes, it's early in the season, but the stakes are high for the 2027 NFL Draft. Getting the first pick opens up all avenues for the Dolphins: They could take a quarterback they prefer, trade the pick to a desperate team and stock the roster, sit tight and take otherworldly receiver prospect Jeremiah Smith or even trade down a slot or two to get extra picks and still take Smith.

Tanking is a taboo subject in the NFL but anyone being honest knows that for a team like the 2026 Dolphins, losing heavily in one bad season is the best thing for the future.

The Titans' win was a good thing for the Dolphins.

The Dolphins and Chargers are the last winless teams. While it seems like the Chargers are far better than the Dolphins and won't seriously challenge Miami for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, maybe they are as bad as they've looked. The Chargers are 31st in DVOA , and a distant 32nd in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense. They are ninth in EPA per play allowed on defense, which provides more hope. But overall the Chargers are as bad as their record.

"Obviously 0-6 going into the bye, I did not think I would be up here addressing that question," Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said after a 22-6 loss to the Chiefs , according to the team's site .

The offense is at -0.209 EPA per play, and the Titans are the next worst at -0.133. It wouldn't be a surprise if offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, a popular offseason hire, is removed from that role soon.

"We have to address everything, especially offensively," Harbaugh said. "We're not scoring enough points."

When the Titans were down 13-0 to the Colts at halftime, and eventually 13-6 after three quarters, it looked bleak. The Titans had shown very few signs of being the type of team that could overcome a double-digit deficit to win on the road. But they outscored the Colts 26-7 in the second half to win.

"The players, these kids put in so much work, and this league is hard," Robert Saleh said after his first win as Titans head coach, via the team's site . "We'd been close on a few occasions, and to knock this one out for them, I am much more excited for them than for myself."

It's not like this was a big breakout game. Cam Ward had 102 yards passing. The Titans had 186 yards as a team, while the Colts gained 399. Tennessee had just 11 first downs, the fewest in the NFL in Week 6. But the Titans got their first win, which changes the entire conversation surrounding them for the rest of the season.

The Jets have lost four of five since beating the Titans in Week 1, and have scored 20 points in only one of those five games. New York has been without running back Breece Hall and receiver Adonai Mitchell for multiple games, but there were still questions on offensive coordinator Frank Reich's job security after Sunday's loss to the Patriots.

"I think he's done a good job, I really do," head coach Aaron Glenn told the media Monday . "Obviously there are a number of things we can improve on, from short yardage to two-minute. That goes on me also, when it comes to the defensive side, me and [defensive coordinator Brian] Duker, on some things we have to get better at too."

Glenn might not be able to afford firing another coordinator he picked. After his first season as head coach, he replaced 12 of the 22 assistants from the staff. Demoting or firing Reich after six games would be a terrible look, considering putting together a staff is one of a head coach's top responsibilities.

Losing to the Titans at home, after holding a 13-0 lead, was a season-changing result and in many ways a franchise-changing one. General manager Chris Ballard was fired on Monday morning . The drafting of Anthony Richardson Sr. and the big trade for Sauce Gardner, which cost Indianapolis its 2026 and 2027 first-round picks, were the two most ruinous moves for Ballard.

Head coach Shane Steichen can't feel too comfortable either. It's not just one loss, it's the feeling that at 2-4, the Colts are going nowhere. Team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon said in her statement Monday announcing Ballard's firing that at the start of the season "the sense of urgency has never been higher," and she had to act on that.

The rest of the season will be picking up the pieces from the Titans loss, but it feels like it could get a lot worse.

"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner said, via WISH-TV .

Assuming Jalen Hurts is done for the season due to a diagnosis of blood clots in his lungs , it's hard to see a way for the Eagles to dig out of their hole. The Eagles were unimpressive with Hurts at quarterback, only getting close wins over the Commanders and Titans. Tanner McKee became a cult hero for some good preseason games a couple years ago, but the hot takes surrounding him perhaps replacing Hurts or what general manager Howie Roseman could get in a trade for him have frozen over. McKee, who entered the season third on the depth chart after failing to beat Andy Dalton for the No. 2 spot, had 215 yards on 45 attempts Sunday in a loss to the Panthers. He's not going to save the Eagles' season.

How bad will it get ? Will head coach Nick Sirianni survive? Will multiple stars be traded before the deadline? It seems like that's the only drama left this Eagles season.

The Buccaneers led 16-3 going into the fourth quarter against the Steelers. They were close to winning a couple of games without Baker Mayfield, who is seemingly set to return in Week 7. But the Buccaneers' offense came crashing back to reality and Todd Bowles' defense couldn't get a stop. Tampa Bay gained 47 yards in the fourth quarter and overtime, with two possessions ending in interceptions. The Steelers had five possessions in the fourth quarter and overtime, not counting a kneeldown at the end of the fourth quarter, and scored points on all five (two drives came off those Jalon Daniels interceptions).

The difference in winning that game and losing, falling to 1-5 while the Panthers improved to 3-2 with a win at Philadelphia, is huge.

"We've got no margin for error," Bowles said, according to the team's site .

25. Washington Commanders (1-4-1, LW: 25)

Jayden Daniels throwing the ball away even though it was fourth down and Dan Quinn seemingly not knowing it was fourth down at all says everything that needs to be said about the 2026 Commanders. If that wasn't enough on Monday night, after last week's game-management debacle at the end of overtime against the Giants, the Commanders had to use a timeout with the clock stopped with 3:01 left in the game before a fourth down play. That ended up costing Washington a valuable 40 seconds, as it ran out of time on a comeback attempt in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers. Washington has a bye coming up next, and whatever answers Quinn gives to why he seemingly didn't know it was fourth down will be a big discussion point, not just among fans and media, but also within the organization. It seems like a team in desperate need of a reset.

Nick Rallis was under heat after the first five games. He has been Arizona's defensive coordinator since 2023, survived a head coaching change, and none of his defenses have ranked better than 21st in yards allowed. A slow start to the season with new head coach Mike LaFleur had people wondering if Rallis was close to being replaced.

Rallis bought himself some time. The Cardinals had a shocking win Sunday led by their defense, which held the Rams under 300 yards and to 16 points. The Cardinals kept the pressure on Matthew Stafford and forced him and the Rams' offense into a poor game. That relieves a lot of pressure, and provides hope this season.

"We needed that turnaround," defensive lineman L.J. Collier told the team's site . "We balled today on all fronts."

It's troubling that the Saints allowed J.J. McCarthy to throw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter off the bench and a 34-10 lead turned into a game the Saints almost lost. But as much as we like to believe it should never happen, teams that are up big sometimes let down, and it's hard to get that back if the opponent rallies. Let's assume that's what happened after the Giants benched Jameis Winston.

If we excuse the final 11 minutes, the Saints played their best game in weeks. Tyler Shough shook off a terrible game against the Vikings to throw for three touchdowns. New Orleans rushed for 175 yards. The Saints' defense is why Winston got benched. An upcoming three-game stretch against the Steelers in Paris, then hosting the Browns and Panthers, could change the NFC South race in New Orleans' favor.

The Falcons rallied in the fourth quarter but they were terrible for the first 50 minutes. They trailed the Bears 31-7. The Falcons deserve credit for fighting back. They had a shot to tie it when they had the ball trailing 31-23 in the final minutes, though a sack and a fumble ruined that. But rallies like that after it seems the result of the game has been decided can give false hope. The Falcons were miserable against a questionable Bears defense until that late rally, and Atlanta's defense allowed Caleb Williams to complete 30-of-36 passes for 305 yards.

"I'm obviously proud of how we continue to fight, but to start like we started is really, really disappointing," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said, via the team's site .

The Falcons have had three awful games, two great ones, and one in which they played well but failed at the end against the Ravens. That makes them very hard to judge going forward. One thing is clear: Atlanta can't have another game in which Bijan Robinson gets only nine carries, which is what happened Sunday.

Nobody questioned the Cowboys' offense. Through four games Dallas averaged 30.5 points per game and was third in the NFL in EPA per play, trailing only San Francisco and Buffalo. Then, over the last two games, its offense has disappeared against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, neither of which has a great defense.

The Cowboys are averaging 14.5 points over their last two games and slipped to 19th in EPA per play. Their defense isn't good enough to overcome that.

"Because of the lack of a running game, we're a little bit one-sided and the best way to be on offense as a unit is to have balance," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said, according to ESPN.

The running game is a problem. Dallas has just 98 rushing yards total over the last two games, it has reached 100 yards in a game just once and rank 31st in rushing yards per game. It's also accurate that the Cowboys looked completely unprepared for a blitz-heavy approach from the Packers, and that could be a coaching issue . Perhaps getting the run game going will dissuade future opponents from blitzing on most downs.

The Giants officially have a quarterback controversy, if it's even controversial. J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston and threw for 243 yards in 11 minutes. It would be a surprise if he's not given a start, though perhaps New York wants to wait for his first start with a tough Houston defense up next.

The other weird story from Sunday's loss was Cam Skattebo getting zero carries . He fumbled in overtime against the Commanders in Week 5, but it's hard to believe him not getting a carry was due only to that. It's harder to believe John Harbaugh, who tried to gaslight everyone by saying Skattebo wasn't benched.

The Browns have four very close wins in the final minutes, and the last two victories came in the final 10 seconds. They're 21st in DVOA. In betting terms, they have the longest odds to win the AFC North despite being in first place right now. This is not sustainable, especially with an offense that is 29th in DVOA, which is why they're not higher than 19th. But it is a lot of fun right now in Cleveland .

One thing that shouldn't change is the defense will keep the Browns in games. That unit is ninth in DVOA. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, last season's NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, is a star and his forced fumble on Derrick Henry in the fourth quarter led to a Browns touchdown and turned around the game.

"It's been an unbelievable credit to our team, especially our defense," Browns head coach Todd Monken said, according to the team's site . "Early on, after 10 points, shutting them out and constantly getting us the ball back and giving us a chance to win."

The Raiders caught a very tough part of the schedule after a 3-0 start. They faced the Chiefs, Patriots and Bills, who are a combined 14-3. The Raiders were blown out at New England but led Kansas City in the fourth quarter and were tied with Buffalo in the fourth quarter. A three-game losing streak isn't what the Raiders wanted, but it is not unreasonable. Of course, the team wasn't happy with coming close against top competition.

"We have to find ways to win those games," Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum said, according to the team's site . "To be happy that we're close with teams like that, I don't think that's a good mindset to have."

The Raiders face perhaps the most interesting game of Week 7 as they host a Rams team that is 2-4 and just got embarrassed at home by the Cardinals. The Raiders will be looking to finally break through against a talented team, but that won't be easy.

The 2025 Texans started 0-3, blew out a hapless Titans team, then got a 44-10 win against the Ravens and that led to a 12-5 record and a playoff berth. This season's Texans started 0-4, blew out a hapless Titans team and then got a huge 34-31 win against a good Jaguars team in London. The next four games are vs. Giants, at Chargers, at Browns, vs. Colts. Those teams rank 28th, 31st, 21st and 25th in DVOA. Nothing is guaranteed in the NFL, but there's an opportunity for the Texans to be 6-4 in a month.

The play of C.J. Stroud offers long-term optimism. He led all quarterbacks in EPA per play in Week 6 through Sunday's games, and did so against a Jaguars defense that was playing well. Stroud has been up and down this season, but has generally been good as long as Nico Collins is in the lineup. If he continues to play well, digging out of an 0-4 hole is very possible.

Are the Steelers doing it again? Nothing about them is impressive … except their record. That's a recurring theme for the Steelers in recent seasons. Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 through three quarters on Sunday and came all the way back to win in overtime. They won despite not having a play longer than 19 yards. They averaged 3.9 yards per play.

Aaron Rodgers' performance summed up the day, and the Steelers' start as well. Against Tampa Bay, he had a negative EPA per play and a very low 3.91-yard average depth of target, according to Sumer Sports . Somehow the Steelers got the win. And they're two games over .500 with Rodgers being below average across the board in his age-42 season.

The most telling comment from the Rams' loss probably came from running back Kyren Williams, who seemingly isn't happy that he's sharing snaps with Blake Corum. He was asked why the offense has inconsistent energy.

"Can't tell you, bro," Williams said . "Probably because I'm not out there."

Williams played 72.4% of the snaps against the Cardinals, and Corum did have 60 total yards and a touchdown. It's not like he was ineffective. But the Rams should be frustrated with a 2-4 start, and Williams was willing to share it.

There are many teams that are impossible to rank after six weeks. The Packers were so bad through four weeks, despite a 2-2 record, that plenty of fans wanted Matt LaFleur fired immediately. Through three weeks this season they had lost seven of eight going back to last season. They couldn't run the ball or protect Jordan Love and Green Bay's defense was below average. The Packers barely beat the Buccaneers and Jets, who are a combined 3-9. The first month was bad, and there shouldn't be any revisionist history about that.

Then the last two weeks, the Packers blew out the Bears and Cowboys, and are suddenly 4-2 and on a roll. Had you just watched the last two games and nothing else, you'd think the Packers might be a top-five team at worst. But the first four weeks did happen too. The Packers still struggle mightily to run the ball and to protect Love, though the QB was masterful against pressure on Sunday night. Green Bay, like many other teams this season, is hard to figure out.

Bryce Young continues to shine. He had 281 passing yards and two touchdowns against a good Eagles defense. He's up to 1,549 yards, 11 touchdowns and two interceptions for the season. It's a stunning turnaround.

"It says that man should be winning MVP," Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble, who had both touchdown catches against the Eagles, told the team's site. "He's the best quarterback in the league, man. He's balling."

While the Buffalo Bills might argue that Josh Allen is the best QB in the league, he is playing very well. And he has help: Chuba Hubbard rushed for 120 yards, Tremble caught two touchdowns, and Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan combined for 183 yards. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik took over play-calling duties this season and if this production continues he'll be a hot name on the head-coaching carousel next offseason.

If you haven't watched a game or looked at any stats, you'd think the Broncos are having a great season. They're 4-2 against the second-toughest schedule in the NFL, according to DVOA. Their group of quality wins against the Jaguars, Rams and Seahawks is arguably the best in the league.

That's what makes the Broncos so confusing. They have looked bad for most of this season, especially on offense, but find ways to win games. Quarterback Bo Nix's 4.9-yard average depth of target is 701st of 701 qualified quarterback seasons through six weeks across the last 20 years, according to CBS Sports' Doug Clawson . The offense has been beyond broken, no matter who is calling plays. Yet, they're 4-2 against a brutal schedule and that's hard to argue with.

The Lions' bye was well timed. The next two weeks they host the Packers and Vikings. Those two games will determine if they're a factor in a tough NFC North race.

They are also getting reinforcements. Center Cade Mays and safety Brian Branch are expected to return from injuries. The Branch return is very interesting for a defense that needs help, though Branch can't be guaranteed to solve all problems as he comes off a torn Achilles. When healthy, Branch is a difference maker. It remains to be seen if the injury cost him any explosiveness. He won't get a full snap share right away, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Monday. But just having him and Mays back gives the Lions hope that they can make a statement in the division race over the next two games.

The Bengals' first game after their bye is huge as they face the Ravens in Baltimore. Lamar Jackson's health will be the biggest topic of the week in Baltimore and Cincinnati.

The good news for the Bengals is that Joe Burrow has been cooking. He has 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions. His 71.4% completion percentage would be the best of his career for a full season. His 104.4 passer rating would be the third-best of his career. The best stat might be that he has been sacked nine times which ranks 22nd in the league. Right tackle Amarius Mims becoming one of the NFL's best offensive linemen is a big reason.

The Jaguars looked very good through four weeks, but the London trip was not great for them. They were very lucky to escape with a 1-1 record on the trip, thanks to Philadelphia's game-management error gifting Jacksonville a last-second field goal to win. Its defense had a big letdown against Houston as it allowed C.J. Stroud to pick apart the Jaguars. Instead of knocking the Texans out of the AFC South race, Houston now lingers with an easy four-game stretch of its schedule coming up. It was a very disappointing outcome for a team that looked like it was one of the few to look like a trustworthy contender after the season's first month.

Still, a 4-2 start isn't a bad outcome, and the Jaguars don't seem concerned.

"I've got a lot of confidence in this team," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said after the game . "We didn't get the result we wanted. We're not going to change a thing about our process."

Seattle is another tough team to rank. Logically, the Seahawks are much better than their 3-3 record. However, their flaws are evident and it's clear they are not the same level as last season. That was going to be hard to replicate after a dominant, special championship season, but it's still disappointing to see the offense bogged down without a reliable running game (letting Kenneth Walker III walk in free agency looks worse each week) and much in the passing game aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

All of the offensive issues have affected Sam Darnold, who is turning it over way too much. His overtime interception against a Broncos team that could not move the ball on offense cost the Seahawks that game. It's not all his fault but after seven interceptions in what amounts to four full games, he has to clean it up.

"I just think it's BS for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said after the loss to the Broncos . "It's not fair to our defense, it's not fair to our special teams group, not fair really to the entire team. I've got to be better that way."

The Patriots lost 13-10 at Seattle in the opener, when they were in position to kick a game-tying field goal at the end. If that turns out different, we're having a much different conversation about the Patriots. They have blown out the Steelers and Raiders, who have had some good moments this season. They won at the Bills. The win over the Jets might not have been dominant but they were up 10 points going into the final minute.

Of course, the Patriots' season turned when Drake Maye started to heat up. Through three games he had 585 yards, one touchdown and six interceptions. In the three games since he has 878 yards, 10 touchdowns and one interception. A.J. Brown is back (though Romeo Doubs went on injured reserve with a shoulder injury ) so the Patriots' offense should continue to flourish.

The 31-23 win over the Falcons wasn't really that close. The Bears let down in the fourth quarter, turning a 31-7 lead into a one-score game. That's not ideal but the way they played through three quarters in Caleb Williams' return was impressive.

Cornerback Kyler Gordon's odd 2026 took a positive turn. Gordon had missed the offseason and the first five games due to a calf injury, prompting questions about his future with the team. In just 17 snaps on Sunday, Gordon had three sacks and one forced a fumble in the final minutes with the Falcons trailing by eight points. He's the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983. He's just the second defensive back in NFL history with three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game, joining Rod Kush of the Houston Oilers in 1985, according to the Bears' site . His playmaking will be welcomed on the Bears' defense.

Jordan Mason's return from a broken thumb, which should happen in Week 7, won't create big headlines but it's important for the Vikings. Aaron Jones Sr. filled in well, but he's 31 years old and asking him to handle almost all of the running back duties was not a long-term plan. Mason and Jones form a good committee, and they can resume their roles. The Vikings face the reeling Colts this week before a four-game stretch that will define their season: at Lions, vs. Bills, at Packers, vs. 49ers (in Mexico City). If they beat the Colts and go 2-2 in the four games that follow, they'll be in great shape.

With so many teams that should have been good this season struggling, it's hard to penalize the Ravens in these rankings too much for a last-second loss with Lamar Jackson out. If Jackson was out for an indefinite period maybe the Ravens' outlook wouldn't be as positive, but he could be back as soon as Week 7. Baltimore is still a very good team that is close to being 6-0. The Ravens need him back, as they face a huge AFC North game against the Bengals. Going 1-1 in two road games with Tyler Huntley at quarterback wasn't the worst outcome, even if Sunday's loss on a field goal as time expired to the Browns was disappointing.

"I think that's one we definitely should've won," safety Kyle Hamilton said, via the team's site . "You let a team stay around, they're going to find momentum. The defense, we've got to go out there and get some stops at the end, ice the game"

Josh Allen had a highlight that will be replayed often through the years, when his career is discussed. Allen was under pressure and at about the 14-yard line he flipped it backhanded almost 20 yards into the end zone to an open Keon Coleman for a touchdown. We've seen the highlights of Brett Favre making those plays for decades and the same should be the same for Allen. It was a masterful improvisation.

"I was just trying to make a play," Allen said, via the team's site . "They play really good defense. Kind of stepped up in the pocket, felt somebody coming from the left side there, stepped back and again, quick eyes saw our guy open and gave him a chance."

It's hard to believe that an offense with Patrick Mahomes at quarterback has been turned over to another player, but Kenneth Walker III's impact on the Chiefs can't be understated. Walker had another 128 yards and two touchdowns on the ground as the Chiefs easily beat the Chargers 22-6. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, even though Kansas City has already had its bye. His 133 rushing yards per game puts him on pace for 2,261 rushing yards. Since 1984, Eric Dickerson has held the NFL's single-season record with 2,105 yards.

Walker's candidacy for MVP will be discussed, but it's still a long shot because voters have turned it into a quarterback award. Adrian Peterson was the last non-quarterback to win and that came back in 2012. The MVP has gone to a quarterback 18 of the last 19 seasons. But if Walker can get to 2,000 yards, it might give him a chance.

The Mike Evans injury is scary for the 49ers, because they don't have much left at receiver. Deebo Samuel Sr. was out on Monday night with a hamstring injury. De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson and Ricky Pearsall are on IR. Brock Purdy is playing very well but he needs something at receiver. The good news was that Evans' injury isn't considered serious and no more testing is needed, according to 49ers coach Mike Shanahan. It's still not out of the question that Evans could miss a little time or that the injury could be an issue that lingers. And the offense without Evans didn't look great on Monday night.

The offense struggled in the second half with 67 net yards, 65 of which came on the first drive of the half. That's hard to believe from a Shanahan-coached team, but the 49ers were playing receivers that were nowhere near their plans when the season started. The 49ers' bad injury luck has been startling, and it could end up affecting what could be a special season.

articles.title: 49ers report card after narrow escape against Commanders on MNF
articles.summary: The 49ers escaped Monday Night Football with their perfect record still in tact.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA — The 49ers escaped Monday Night Football with their perfect record still in tact.

They took extended their lead to 20 points on their first possession of the second half and held for a 23-17 win as the Commanders whittled the lead away with 14 unanswered points after halftime.

Grading the 49ers' closer-than-expected win over Washington, which fell to 1-4-1:

He attained the record with his fifth pass of the night, a screen to Christian McCaffrey for his 1,500th career attempt, and on his next throw, Purdy put the ball where only George Kittle could get to it in the corner of the end zone. The 49ers' opening touchdown only served to set the tone for the rest of Purdy's night, as precise and on-point as any other this season.

Purdy completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown. And to boot, he outgained the Commanders' dual-threat quarterback on the ground, too, with 28 yards on five scrambles.

Missing many of their top receivers, the 49ers put the ball in Christian McCaffrey's hands.

He put it on the ground once but otherwise carried the load for the 49ers offensively in a way that he had yet to in five games this season. After leading the NFL with 413 touches last season, McCaffrey hadn't gotten involved more than 19 times in a game this year.

McCaffrey was responsible for two of the 49ers' three first-half touchdowns and had 82 yards on 16 touches before halftime, more than he had in three of their five previous contests.

San Francisco finished with 29 carries for 126 yards on the ground — 16 for 64 from McCaffrey — against a rush defense that had limited opponents to 3.9 yards per carry entering the game.

Although he acted as the 49ers' offensive engine, McCaffrey gets a demerit for a rare fumble that cost the 49ers points. Linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson punched the ball out of McCaffrey's arms on the edge of the red zone, leading to his first fumble of the season.

McCaffrey has never lost more than one fumble in any of his nine previous seasons.

Mike Evans aggravated a sore Achilles that caused him to miss practice this week and limped to the locker room shortly before halftime, calling into question the 49ers' decision to play him in the first place. Then again, they desperately needed his 94 yards on three first-half catches.

The 49ers' passing game mostly collapsed without Evans in the second half.

McCaffrey hauled in a season-high nine passes, but only for 53 yards. Kittle added five catches for 69 yards. But Purdy didn't complete more than one pass to any other target.

Trent Williams pancaked one defender and Dominic Puni plowed another to open a hole for McCaffrey to cross the goal line untouched for his first touchdown.

The 49ers' line held up well, all things considered. The Commanders entered the game with the second-highest blitz rate in the league and didn't hold back from sending extra rushers, but the 49ers mostly kept Purdy upright — at least as long had someone to throw to.

San Francisco yielded two sacks, both in the second half after Evans left the game.

For the second straight game, the 49ers played without Nick Bosa and it was hardly noticeable.

Osa Odighizuwa, Mykel Williams and Gracen Halton all got home for sacks of Jayden Daniels, who lost more yards (21) on the 49ers' three sacks than he gained on four rush attempts (10).

Romello Height forced an intentional grounding that resulted in a 10-second runoff, leaving the Commanders with one, final play from around midfield, and that one ended with Keion White on top of Daniels for their fourth sack of the evening.

Altogether, the Commanders mustered just 53 yards on 17 carries, an average of 3.1 per attempt, after entering with the NFL's seventh-most efficient ground game (4.7 YPC).

When the 49ers needed a stop most, of course it was Fred Warner who stepped up.

With the Commanders driving down the field late in the fourth quarter, threatening to come all the way back from a 23-3 deficit, Warner wrapped up Rachaad White for an open-field tackle that should have gotten the 49ers off the field. Instead, a penalty on safety Malik Mustapha on the next play extended the Commanders' drive.

Mustapha would earn the ultimate redemption a few plays later, providing the pass defense on Daniels' fourth-down heave to Treylon Burks that gave the 49ers the ball back with 1:54 to go.

The 49ers caught an unfortunate break early when Daniels' top target, Terry McLaurin, had to be carted to the locker room with what appeared to be a serious knee injury.

Still, their defensive backs had a hard time keeping up with Washington's receivers. Stefon Diggs was a frequent problem, and Upton Stout let him get free to convert a fourth-and-5 on Washington's second drive of the second half, which ended in a touchdown.

A defense that has allowed the fewest explosive plays in the NFL was torched for gains of 27, 29 and 30 yards after coverages broke down. Daniels didn't beat them with his feet, but he proved to be the toughest test yet for the 49ers' secondary, which allowed him to complete 29 of40 passes for 300 yards, posting the highest passer rating of any quarterback to face the 49ers this season (110.7).

They definitely have an extra-point issue.

McCaffrey's fumble inside the red zone left at least six points on the board, and the 49ers cost themselves another point when Eddy Pineiro's point-after attempt sailed wide right.

The missed PAT was Pineiro's third this season and his seventh in 58 attempts since the 49ers signed him in Week 2 of last season. He was good from 33 to improve to 34-of-38 in his San Francisco career when three points are on the line, opposed to one.

Pineiro's job status should still be more secure than Jacob Cowing, who muffed a punt return for the second week in a row. Although the 49ers recovered this one, Cowing's butterfingers backed them up on their 7-yard line, leading to the Commanders taking over on a short field.
