articles.title: 49ers Survive Late Scare to Stay Undefeated With Win Over Commanders
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers continued their undefeated start to the 2026 NFL season Monday night, defeating the Washington Commanders 23-17 at Levi’s Stadium. Sa...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers continued their undefeated start to the 2026 NFL season Monday night, defeating the Washington Commanders 23-17 at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco dominated the first half before nearly allowing a comfortable lead to slip away, ultimately relying on its defense to secure another victory.

The win improved the 49ers to 6-0, giving them their best start since the 2019 season, when they reached the Super Bowl. However, the second half struggles showed that San Francisco still has areas to address despite its impressive record.

Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey Lead the Offense

Quarterback Brock Purdy got San Francisco off to a fast start, connecting with tight end George Kittle for an 11 yard touchdown to cap the opening drive. Purdy consistently moved the offense downfield early, finishing with 264 passing yards and one touchdown while completing 21 of 29 attempts.

Running back Christian McCaffrey also played a major role in the victory. McCaffrey scored twice on one-yard touchdown runs, helping the 49ers establish control and put Washington in an early hole.

San Francisco entered halftime with a commanding 20-3 advantage after outgaining Washington 303-90 in the opening two quarters. The 49ers added a 33 yard field goal from Eddy Piñeiro in the third quarter to extend their lead to 23-3.

Wide receiver Mike Evans contributed three receptions for 94 yards before leaving with an aggravated Achilles injury just before halftime. His departure became a significant concern as the 49ers struggled to generate offense after the break.

Washington refused to go away quietly. Quarterback Jayden Daniels sparked the comeback with a one-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs late in the third quarter. Daniels then connected with Rachaad White for a nine-yard touchdown in the fourth, cutting the deficit to 23-17.

The Commanders suddenly had an opportunity to steal the game, putting pressure on a San Francisco offense that struggled to sustain drives in the second half.

Washington reached the 49ers' 17-yard line with less than two minutes remaining, but safety Malik Mustapha delivered a crucial pass breakup on fourth down to preserve the lead.

The Commanders received one final opportunity, moving into San Francisco territory in the closing seconds. However, Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo brought Daniels down for a game-ending sack.

The 49ers escaped with the victory, but their second-half performance will give head coach Kyle Shanahan plenty to review. San Francisco's offense stalled, while penalties and defensive breakdowns allowed Washington back into the contest.

Despite the late scare, the 49ers remain unbeaten at 6-0. Their ability to win a close game could prove valuable as the season continues, but maintaining their early dominance for four quarters will be essential if they hope to remain among the NFL's elite.

articles.title: Commanders star Terry McLaurin carted off after knee injury early in loss to 49ers
articles.summary: Terry McLaurin was carted off in an air cast after going down early on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin early Monday night after he went down with what appears to be a significant knee injury.

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when he suddenly fell near the sideline at Levi's Stadium. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in a lot of pain.

A cart eventually came out for McLaurin, and he hopped up and onto the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast. Players from both teams then saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said after the contest that they didn't have any details, but they were concerned that the injury was significant.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards in the contest before he went down.

McLaurin entered Monday with 203 receiving yards and a single touchdown in four games this season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders. He missed the team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury he suffered at practice before that contest before returning the following week.

While it's unclear how long McLaurin may be sidelined, the injury is a tough sign for a Commanders group that is struggling this season. The Commanders sit at just 1-4-1, which has them in last in the NFC East race. While they rallied a bit late and had a good look at the win down the stretch on Monday night, they couldn't quite pull it off.

The win pushed the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 on the year, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, are also still undefeated.

The NFC East is still wide open, so the Commanders aren't completely out of the playoff hunt yet despite their rough start. But losing a target like McLaurin for a substantial amount of time is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels as they approach the midway point of the season.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans' injury was Achilles soreness that won't require more testing
articles.summary: Mike Evans came up slowly after making a huge grab just before halftime on Monday night.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers lost star wide receiver Mike Evans early on Monday night due to Achilles soreness, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters postgame .

Evans, just before halftime of the Niners' 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders , caught a 16-yard pass from Brock Purdy to convert a first down and put the 49ers into scoring position. Evans dove to make the grab.

Evans was clearly shaken up after the catch. He was slow to walk off the field, and he was spotted stretching out his leg in the tunnel at Levi's Stadium.

Evans had been dealing with an Achilles injury, and was questionable entering the contest with that and a rib injury.

Shanahan said he didn't believe the injury will require further testing.

Evans had three catches for 94 yards before he went down. The team ruled Evans out just after halftime.

The injury was the second significant one to impact a wide receiver on Monday night. Commanders star Terry McLaurin was carted off the field in the first quarter after his left knee buckled. He was in a full air cast, and the team quickly ruled him out with a knee injury.

The 49ers took a 20-3 lead at halftime. Christian McCaffrey scored both of their touchdowns, including a 1-yard run just a few plays after Evans left the contest.

Evans is in his first season with the 49ers. He spent his first 12 seasons in the league with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and he racked up 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons before that streak was cut shot last year due to various injuries. He signed a three-year deal with the 49ers this past offseason, and entered Monday's contest with 326 receiving yards and three touchdowns through five games.

Though Washington rallied in the second half, and had a look to grab the win down the stretch, the 49ers held on to take the six-point win . That pushed them to 6-0, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Minnesota Vikings (5-0) and Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), are also still undefeated. The Commanders fell to 1-4-1.

While the 49ers still haven't lost, losing Evans for any substantial amount of time will be a significant hit to their offense. The way they slowed down in the second half on Monday night was a perfect example of that.

articles.title: ‘Very Weird,’ ‘People Will Write Anything’ — NFL Fans Defend Madison Beer After Columnist Blames Her for Justin Herbert’s Struggles
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a nightmare start in the 2026 NFL season. Sunday’s 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs dropped them to 0-6, leaving their...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a nightmare start in the 2026 NFL season. Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs dropped them to 0-6, leaving their playoff hopes hanging by a thread.

With the team struggling to get going, quarterback Justin Herbert has also faced his share of criticism. But the conversation has gone beyond the field.

Sports columnist Ethan Strauss recently suggested that Herbert's relationship with his fiancée, pop singer Madison Beer, could be affecting his performance. That theory hasn't sat well with many fans and analysts, who have been quick to push back.

NFL Analyst and Fans Fire Back at Madison Beer Narrative

Strauss sparked the debate with an article, titled "The Justin Herbert Madison Beer Factor: Everyone's Thinking It. Nobody's Writing It."

In his piece, Strauss discussed how the media has covered the Chargers' disappointing season. While traditional reporters have largely focused on the team's on-field struggles, some online commentators have questioned whether Herbert's relationship with Beer has become a distraction.

The columnist referenced Shannon Sharpe and Chad Johnson's discussion on "Nightcap," where the duo added to the debate over whether Beer is contributing to Herbert's struggles.

Former NFL running back Leonard Fournette has also weighed in . Speaking on his podcast, he suggested that Herbert's relationship was affecting his performance, saying, "Love is holding [Herbert] back."

Strauss acknowledged that blaming Beer for Herbert's struggles might be an oversimplification, but argued that a high-profile relationship could still affect a quarterback.

"While it's probably silly to believe that a quarterback's focus might be derailed by the incandescent attractiveness of his significant other, it's less silly to wonder if a high-profile relationship complicates his existence," he wrote.

Strauss also questioned whether coach Jim Harbaugh is holding Herbert accountable, particularly after the quarterback missed voluntary workouts to visit Beer during her European tour.

However, not everyone agrees with Strauss' argument, and NFL analyst Marcus Mosher was among those who pushed back. Rather than blaming Herbert's relationship with Beer, Mosher pointed to the Chargers' injury problems as a more plausible explanation for the quarterback's struggles.

"All this time, I thought the Chargers losing four offensive linemen and their No. 1 wide receiver was the reason why Justin Herbert is struggling. I never thought about blaming his girlfriend. Shows how little I know about football," Mosher wrote sarcastically .

As Mosher pointed out, injuries have taken a toll on the Chargers' offensive line. Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt, Kayode Awosika, Trey Pipkins III and Trevor Penning have all dealt with injuries, leaving the team short on options up front.

Wide receiver Ladd McConkey was also evaluated for a concussion during Sunday's loss to Kansas City, further compounding the Chargers' offensive struggles.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Several fans took to social media to defend Beer and call out Strauss' take. One X user wrote, "It's crazy that people still take this guy seriously. You would think that all his podcasts with Richard Hanania would've given people a clue."

A second fan kept it brief: "People will write anything."

A third questioned the logic behind blaming Herbert's fiancée for the team's struggles, writing, "Yeah, because her fiancé and his team playing like [expletive] is her fault?"

Others argued that the Chargers' offensive line woes and coaching decisions were far more deserving of criticism.

"Has to be the stupidest take ever. We all see him have zero pockets and have untouched rushers every snap, while his wide receivers drop passes left and right. Mike McDaniel is washed as a play caller, and five rookie offensive linemen are a mismanagement of a roster. Go make a trade and get some vet OL," one commenter wrote.

Another X user was equally unimpressed with the discussion, calling it "Very weird 'journalism.'"

Justin Herbert Looks to Turn Things Around

Herbert's performance this season has been abysmal, to say the least. Through six games, he has thrown five touchdown passes and eight interceptions while totaling 1,141 passing yards.

The 28-year-old QB ranks dead last among the league's quarterbacks at No. 34, with a PFN QB Impact Score of 61.0.

Herbert has yet to throw for more than 230 yards or record multiple touchdown passes in a game this season. The offensive line's struggles haven't helped, either, as he has been sacked 21 times in six games.

Herbert certainly needs to play better, but the Chargers' injury woes and inconsistent offense have also played a major role in their disappointing start. Blaming Beer for the team's struggles does little to address the issues holding the team back.

The Chargers will now get a bye week before facing the Los Angeles Rams in Week 8.

articles.title: Former Seahawks WR Signs With Steelers to Rejoin Aaron Rodgers: Report
articles.summary: A former Seattle Seahawks wide receiver is heading back to familiar territory after another short-lived NFL stop. Veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling plans to s...
articles.body:
A former Seattle Seahawks wide receiver is heading back to familiar territory after another short-lived NFL stop.

Veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling plans to sign with the Pittsburgh Steelers, according to a report from The Athletic's Mike DeFabo. The expectation is that the 32-year-old will begin on Pittsburgh's practice squad.

The move reunites Valdes-Scantling with quarterback Aaron Rodgers and puts him back alongside former Seahawks star DK Metcalf .

Interestingly, Valdes-Scantling was originally brought to Seattle in March 2025 to help replace the speed lost when the Seahawks traded Metcalf to Pittsburgh.

Following an unsuccessful stint with the Los Angeles Chargers , Valdes-Scantling is preparing for a shot with the Steelers.

Valdes-Scantling's time in Seattle never unfolded as originally planned.

The Seahawks signed the veteran to a one-year contract worth up to $5.5 million in March 2025, with $3 million guaranteed, hoping his downfield speed could complement Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp .

Playing under offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak with the New Orleans Saints in 2024, Valdes-Scantling caught 17 passes for 385 yards and four touchdowns across eight games. His 22.6 yards per reception represented a career high.

However, the receiver never made Seattle's regular-season roster.

The Seahawks released Valdes-Scantling on August 26, 2025, after rookie Tory Horton emerged as a more promising deep threat during training camp.

Seattle also elected to retain Jake Bobo , Dareke Young and Cody White , whose blocking and special teams contributions gave them an advantage.

General manager John Schneider subsequently explained that the decision reflected the competition at receiver rather than a lack of effort from Valdes-Scantling.

"MVS, he came in and did a nice job and competed," Schneider said through the team's official website.

Schneider added that Seattle's other receivers had simply moved ahead of him, with Horton's speed giving the offense a similar weapon.

Ultimately, Valdes-Scantling departed without appearing in a regular-season game for the Seahawks, despite beginning the offseason as a potential No. 3 receiver.

Valdes-Scantling's departure from Seattle started a winding chapter in his NFL career.

He joined the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, recording four receptions for 40 yards across five games before eventually landing in Pittsburgh.

His production improved with the Steelers, where he caught 10 passes for 80 yards and one touchdown in five appearances.

That familiarity with Rodgers is important.

The two previously spent four seasons together with the Green Bay Packers from 2018 through 2021, during which Valdes-Scantling established himself as a legitimate deep-ball threat.

The veteran also won two Super Bowl championships with the Kansas City Chiefs before moving between several teams.

His latest stop with the Chargers proved brief. Valdes-Scantling appeared in three games this season, collecting two receptions for 22 yards before Los Angeles released him October 17 .

Pittsburgh, though, has a pressing need for receiver depth.

Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. are on injured reserve, leaving Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard to shoulder additional responsibilities.

Both receivers caught 11 passes during Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 18.

But Valdes-Scantling makes sense because he can work with a quarterback who knows his strengths.

articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys could get some good injury news coming in this week if Cobie Durant can make it back for Week 7. The post Cowboys Get Good News on Injured...
articles.body:
It has not been difficult in recent weeks to batter the Dallas Cowboys' defense, either with sharp-witted barbs on social media, or on an actual NFL field with 11 even half-decent offensive players. It's not been a difficult group to push around, ranked 30th in the league in points allowed after Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers in Green Bay, and rated No. 30 among NFL defenses by Pro Football Focus. But in finding fault with this unit, it is worth remembering that much of the back line–including starting corner Cobie Durant, starting safety Jalen Thompson and his backup, PJ Locke–has been lodged on the injured reserve for much of the season so far.

But there is some hope, as we move forward in the season, that we'll start to see some of those players return. That does not mean the Cowboys defense necessarily would be vastly improved. It should, though, set the group up to start mending its ways after a brutal start.

Cowboys Could Have a Decision on Cobie Durant

Locke and Thompson are not due back this week, but could return for Week 8 when their injured reserve time runs up. But there was good news out at The Star when coach Brian Schottenheimer met with reporters in the wake of the Packers loss. Durant, who has been out with a hamstring injury for four weeks, could be back on Monday night for the Cowboys' game against the Eagles.

Said Schottenheimer: "Trending up. Getting him moving a little bit these next couple of days. But he is trending to play."

Schottenheimer added that DeMarvion Overshown could return this week, which would be big because Dee Winters will be out with an Achilles tendon injury.

Getting Durant back would be big, though it could force a tough choice for the Cowboys, who have brought in Joey Porter Jr. to be a starting corner on one boundary while Durant has been out. Durant would be an upgrade over struggling All-Pro DaRon Bland on the other boundary, but will the Cowboys have the stomach to bench their $90 million corner for Durant? That remains to be seen.

articles.title: Dan Quinn Explains 4th Down Confusion After Viral Video During Commanders' Loss to 49ers
articles.summary: During the second quarter of Monday night's contest between the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn appeared to be confused about what down it was.
articles.body:
During the second quarter of Monday night's contest between the Washington Commanders and San Francisco 49ers, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn appeared to be confused about what down it was.

Instead of kicking the field goal in 49ers' territory while trailing 13-3, the Commanders went for it and turned it over on downs. Cameras showed Quinn appearing confused , which led some to believe he didn't know it was fourth down.

After the game, he explained that wasn't the case.

"Definitely knew it was fourth down," he told reporters. "We were going for it... We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game. I didn't think it was going to be a 17-14 game; I thought it was probably gonna be a 28-30 game."

The Commanders went on to lose the game 23-17, so it's hard to say whether it would have made a difference if Washington took the field goal.

Regardless, the Commanders are now 1-4-1, and their playoff hopes are dwindling quickly. Quinn is entering hot-seat territory and can't afford to make any big mistakes moving forward.

articles.title: 49ers sputter in second half after Mike Evans' injury but hold on to beat Commanders to improve to 6-0
articles.summary: The 49ers had a big lead, but the Commanders got back in the game.
articles.body: At some point, the San Francisco 49ers' injuries might bring them down. It almost happened in the second half on Monday night. For now, San Francisco's perfect season rolls on. The 49ers raced out to a 20-point lead and it looked like they would cruise to an easy win over the Washington Commanders. But San Francisco's offense stalled with No. 1 receiver Mike Evans sidelined with an Achilles injury he suffered late in the first half, allowing the Commanders to get back in the game. The Niners' defense, which has been a big surprise all season, came up with two big stops in the final two minutes to seal the 23-17 win. The 49ers improved to 6-0 to start the season. Treylon Burks couldn't haul in a fourth-down pass at the goal line as safety Malik Mustapha, who made a huge hit on a run the previous play, slammed him to the ground. FANTASTIC PBU TO PREVENT THE TD ‼️WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hMlXf1fdwc— NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 Washington got one more shot after forcing a punt, but an intentional grounding penalty set the Commanders back and then the 49ers ended the game on a sack. Brock Purdy played well in the first half, as he has all season, but he needs some help. The 49ers are depleted at receiver and it showed in the second half. That allowed the Commanders to get back in it. Washington hurt themselves, particularly with a facemask penalty that negated a touchdown with a little more than four minutes remaining. Jeremy McNichols had a TD here that was wiped away from Chris Paul’s facemask penalty Heartbreaking pic.twitter.com/bvk5eSwiYt— brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 20, 2026 The 49ers look like the best team in football about one-third through the season. It has been a great start, but the injuries are becoming a real concern. The Niners have been the unluckiest team when it comes to injuries for a few seasons, and the bad fortune hasn't stopped. Mike Evans injured in first halfIt wouldn't be a 49ers game without a key injury. Evans, who came into the game with injuries to his ribs and Achilles tendon, left Monday night's game due to the Achilles. He stayed down after a catch late in the second quarter and went straight to the locker room with athletic trainers. He was ruled out of the game by the team.The 49ers are getting desperately thin at receiver and the injury to Evans, who has made an immediate impact on San Francisco's offense, would be a big blow if he has to miss time. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that he didn’t expect the injury to be long-term.Still, it's still a lingering issue for a 33-year-old receiver. And a glimpse at the 49ers’ offense without Evans wasn't pretty.The 49ers slowed down on offense in the second half without Evans and the Commanders got back in the game. Jayden Daniels hit Rachaad White on a touchdown pass with 9:22 left and suddenly Washington had cut San Francisco's lead to 23-17. San Francisco had led 23-3 late in the third quarter. The Commanders forced a quick punt after that and had the ball with a chance to take the lead with 7:46 to go. It looked like an easy night for the 49ers, but Washington was putting San Francisco's perfect record in jeopardy. Second half tightens upOnce Washington started getting momentum, the Commanders were hard to stop. Daniels hadn't had a great night, including strangely throwing the ball away on a fourth down in the first half, but he helped get his team back in the game. He did so without top receiver Terry McLaurin, who was lost in the first half when he was carted off due to a knee injury. The Commanders seemingly took the lead with a little more than four minutes left on a Jeremy McNichols touchdown run, but there was a facemask penalty on Washington guard Chris Paul that negated the score. The 49ers had a big penalty of their own later, when a fourth-down sack was wiped off the board due to an illegal contact penalty that gave Washington a first down. San Francisco came up with the plays it needed, with Mustapha having two big hits on third and fourth down. Washington wasn't finished. It forced a three-and-out and got the ball back with less than a minute to go, but no timeouts. A fair catch interference call helped with field position. The Commanders were running out of time but a 17-yard catch by rookie receiver Antonio Williams got the ball to San Francisco's 28-yard line. But an intentional grounding penalty on Daniels was a crushing blow, especially since there was a 10-second runoff, leaving only six seconds on the clock. A sack on the final play sealed the win.The 49ers survived a scare. Even a great season isn't always going to pretty. And it looks like it could be a memorable year for the 49ers. The injury issues might be the biggest threat to stopping them.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers beat Washington Commanders to stay unbeaten as Brock Purdy becomes highest-rated passer in NFL history
articles.summary: Brock Purdy became the highest-rated passer in NFL history as he completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown to lead the San Francisco 49ers to victory over the Washington Commanders, improving their perfect record to 6-0 to start the season
articles.body:
The Niners followed up an emotional win last week at division rival Seattle by building a 20-point lead and holding off the Commanders (1-4-1) with two late defensive stops.

Jayden Daniels threw two touchdown passes in the second half to cut a 20-point deficit to 23-17, but Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass to Treylon Burks near the goal line with 1:54 to play to preserve the lead.

Washington got the ball back at its 46 with 52 seconds remaining and moved down to the 28 before Daniels was called for intentional grounding, giving the Commanders one last play from the 40. Daniels was then sacked by Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo before he could throw up a desperation pass.

"You're not always happy exactly with how some of the stuff was frustrating, but real proud of the guys for just the competitive stamina to keep it going all game," said head coach Kyle Shanahan. "I was really proud of the defense for finding a way to overcome."

The Niners extended their best start of a season since winning their first eight games in 2019 on the way to a Super Bowl appearance.

Washington lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin to a left knee injury that required an air cast before he was carted off in the first quarter.

Purdy started the game fast with a 24-yard strike to Mike Evans on the third play of the game and an 11-yard touchdown to George Kittle to finish that drive. Evans exited the game later in the first half with Achilles tendinitis.

Purdy went 21 for 29 for 264 yards and officially became the highest-rated passer in NFL history as he passed the 1,500-attempt threshold to qualify. His 105.6 rating is ahead of Lamar Jackson's 102.7.

The Commanders were unable to bounce back from last week's tie against the New York Giants, when they mismanaged the clock in overtime to cost them a chance at a game-winning field goal.

The game was one-sided early with the 49ers scoring touchdowns on the first two drives on Purdy's pass to Kittle and a 1-yard run by McCaffrey.

San Francisco expanded the lead to 20-3 late in the half on McCaffrey's second touchdown run as the Niners gained as many first downs (17) in the first half as the Commanders ran plays.

The 49ers outgained Washington 303 yards to 90 in the half with Washington's best chance at scoring a touchdown in the first half ending when Daniels threw the ball away on fourth-and-2 from the 13.

articles.title: Bill Belichick to the Cowboys? Dallas emerges as a potential landing spot amid NFL return speculation
articles.summary: Dallas sits at 2-4, and a Monday radio segment has already linked Bill Belichick to the Cowboys job.
articles.body: Dallas sits at 2-4, and a Monday radio segment has already linked Bill Belichick to the Cowboys job. The Packers beat Dallas 23-13 on Sunday, which dropped Brian Schottenheimer to 9-13-1 as a head coach. Belichick, let go by the Patriots after the 2023 season, owns six Super Bowl rings. Former Cowboys scout Bryan Broaddus raised the idea on 105.3 The Fan, pointing to Belichick’s 4-2 start at North Carolina. Stephen Jones, meanwhile, said the team still backs Schottenheimer. Nothing suggests a change is close. For now, this is talk, not a plan.Bill Belichick’s case for the Cowboys jobThe résumé gap is the whole point. Belichick has 333 NFL wins as a head coach. The Patriots let him go after 2023, and he has since begun turning around a wayward North Carolina program. Schottenheimer had never been a head coach when Dallas promoted him from offensive coordinator to replace Mike McCarthy before the 2025 season. Talk of a Belichick pursuit existed back then too, but it never turned into anything real.Broaddus said, “Belichick has actually got North Carolina playing well.” He then wondered if that was Belichick’s road back to the NFL. The Tar Heels are 4-2.The station’s Gavin Dawson called Belichick the best-case scenario for Cowboys fans if Dallas ever moved on from Schottenheimer. The Joneses have long admired him, and Dawson said Belichick matches the criteria Jerry Jones wants in a hire. He did not wave away the doubts, though. Dawson worried Belichick might be outdated and brought up the strange bits he ran with his Patriots staff near the end. Then he gave the counterpoint. Belichick is getting results.Why Dallas is unlikely to make the callA longshot is the kind word for it. Dallas is 2-4, yes, and Schottenheimer’s 9-13-1 record is thin for a franchise that expects playoff runs. But a bad October is not a firing, and the front office is saying so.Stephen Jones gave no sign of wavering on Monday. Asked whether the team still stands behind Schottenheimer, he said absolutely. He added that he and Jerry feel good about the coaching staff, which still has to evolve before the wins arrive.Belichick’s own situation is messy too. His UNC program has dealt with scandals and resignations in his first two years, so any NFL team calling him would be weighing baggage along with the wins. And there is the matter of control. Belichick had the last word on football decisions in New England, and Jerry Jones has always kept it in Dallas. The station itself asked on X whether Belichick could work under Jones. That may be a bigger obstacle than any record.A change would have to come first, and Jones’s words point the other way. articles.summary: Another wacky week of NFL action is in the books, and as we head into Week 7, it's getting harder to tell which teams are actually good and which are not.
articles.body:
Another wacky week of NFL action is in the books, and as we head into Week 7, it's getting harder to tell which teams are actually good and which are not.

Things have been a little easier to predict in fantasy, though injuries and bye weeks have regularly taken away top options. Caleb Williams made his return in Week 6, but Jalen Hurts, Lamar Jackson, Saquon Barkley, and Tyler Warren were among the top stars out with injuries.

In Week 7, the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will be on bye.

Managers will likely need to rely on at least a few second-tier stars this week. Here, you'll find some early start/sit recommendations, along with a few potential waiver-wire targets to consider for point-per-reception (PPR) scoring leagues.

Start: Bucky Irving, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers blew a 13-point fourth-quarter lead to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, and part of the problem was that they couldn't sustain their ground game when trying to bleed the clock.

Starting back Bucky Irving was held to just 46 yards on 19 carries, a stat line that undoubtedly disappointed fantasy managers. He wasn't heavily involved in the passing game either and finished with just two catches for three yards.

While managers will want to flush Irving's Week 6 performance, they should be able to trust him in Week 7. Tampa will host the rival Carolina Panthers in a pivotal game that should heavily feature Irving in the offensive game plan.

The Panthers rank dead-last in yards per carry allowed and have surrendered an average of 29.1 fantasy points to opposing backfields.

Sit: MarShawn Lloyd, RB, Green Bay Packers

Two weeks ago, MarShawn Lloyd had a strong outing against the Chicago Bears, finishing with 16.7 fantasy points. Most thought he would shine against a bad Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 6, but he did not.

Lloyd briefly left the game after taking a big hit but was a bit player from the onset. He finished with eight carries for just 10 yards and no receptions.

Now, there's a chance that Josh Jacobs will return to the Green Bay Packers' backfield, as he's been removed from the commissioner's exempt list. Even if Jacobs isn't in the lineup, it's impossible to trust Lloyd with Pierre Strong, Savion Williams, and Kaleb Johnson getting opportunities.

It'll be a tough matchup for Packers backs anyway, as the Detroit Lions have surrendered an average of just 16.8 fantasy points to opposing backfields.

Start: DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

It appears that the Philadelphia Eagles will be without Hurts for the remainder of the season, as he has been diagnosed with blood clots in both lungs, according to The Athletic . This means that the Eagles are likely to rely on quarterback Tanner McKee for the foreseeable future.

McKee wasn't great in Philly's Week 6 loss to the Panthers. However, he did find receiver DeVonta Smith early and often. In Smith's return from a hamstring injury, he caught seven passes for 75 yards and a touchdown.

Managers should be able to rely on Smith, even with McKee behind center. He's the focal point of the passing attack, and he has a terrific matchup against the Cowboys this week.

However, Rice's injury isn't expected to be a long-term issue, and Worthy hasn't been a steady fantasy producer. While he's reached double-digit fantasy points in three of five outings, he's also delivered fewer than five points twice.

Worthy also has a fairly limited ceiling, even in PPR leagues, as he has yet to reach 15 fantasy points in a game.

articles.title: Germie Bernard and the Best Week 7 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football regular season is reaching the halfway mark, making Week 7 an ideal time to review your lineup and make some significant adjustments.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football regular season is reaching the halfway mark, making Week 7 an ideal time to review your lineup and make some significant adjustments.

Sleepers and breakout candidates who haven't seen the field or contributed with any regularity should be long gone at this point. Potential stars who should have produced by now—such as Cam Skattebo and Brian Thomas Jr.—can also go. Tying up valuable roster spots with these disappointing players is no longer reasonable, not with so many consistent performers and high-upside players still up for grabs in free agency.

Although there may not be many clear league-winners lurking in the free-agent pool right now, there is still tons of talent worth turning over the bottom of your roster for. With that in mind, let's highlight the top waiver-wire targets for Week 7.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings (51 Percent Rostered)

Murray hasn't been putting up QB1-tier numbers over his first four games with the Vikings, but he did deliver his best performance of 2026 right before the team's Week 6 bye.

That 18.3-point effort in a win over the New Orleans Saints makes him an intriguing option for managers searching for a quarterback upgrade.

All the pieces are in place for Murray to build on his season-best showing. Justin Jefferson (ankle) returned to the lineup in Week 5 after missing a game and posted a 6/79/1 line on seven targets, while tight end T.J. Hockenson (concussion) should be back after an explosive 13-catch, 119-receiving yard showing in his last full game.

These weapons, coupled with Murray's rushing ability, provide a safe fantasy floor.

The schedule is also highly favorable for the signal-caller. Minnesota is set to square off against several weak defenses in the coming month, starting with the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. After that comes a pair of teams in the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills that both rank bottom-three in fantasy points allowed to opposing passers.

For this reason, Murray is the best waiver choice for managers needing a longer-term option at the QB position.

Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh Steelers (42 Percent Rostered)

Rodgers has become a dependable fantasy option, recording four consecutive top-12 finishes entering Week 7. Although his latest performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers wasn't his most efficient, he still helped his managers with another low-end QB1 showing.

The veteran completed a season-high 33 of 49 pass attempts for 253 yards and two touchdowns in Week 6, finishing with 17 fantasy points. While his 5.2 yards per attempt left something to be desired, Rodgers slung the rock enough to move the needle.

Expect the 42-year-old to continue airing it out when the Steelers take on the New Orleans Saints in Paris this weekend. The contest has the makings of a high-scoring affair, setting Rodgers up to work as a strong one-week rental before landing back on the free-agent scrap heap during his Week 8 bye.

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (1 Percent Rostered)

McCarthy saw his first extended action as a Giant on Sunday, coming in to relieve an ineffective Jameis Winston.

Even more shocking, the third-year QB's presence provided a massive offensive spark, with McCarthy leading a remarkable fourth-quarter comeback attempt that brought the G-Men within a touchdown after trailing by 24 points.

Despite playing just a single quarter, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception, adding 26 rushing yards on two carries. He delivered a surprising top-12 fantasy finish, demonstrating the upside that made him a top-10 pick in the 2024 draft.

Head coach John Harbaugh has thus far declined to name a starter for a Week 7 battle against the Houston Texans, but McCarthy should get serious consideration after such an impressive display.

Managers in deeper formats seeking a high-upside passer could do worse than rolling the dice on McCarthy earning New York's QB1 role and performing at a high level in the back half of the season.

Kendre Miller, New Orleans Saints (34 Percent Rostered)

Miller is the healthiest Saints running back right now, with Travis Etienne Jr. languishing on the IR and Alvin Kamara nursing a back injury. That availability and opportunity make him one of the top waiver-wire targets for Week 7.

While Kamara did play in Week 6 and salvaged his day with a touchdown reception, the veteran star spent some time in the blue medical tent and had just nine touches in total. Miller was the preferred rushing option for much of Sunday's win over the New York Giants, generating 70 yards on a season-high 20 totes.

Miller doesn't get many looks in the passing game, is mostly utilized on early downs and will likely experience a huge workload reduction once Etienne returns, but that won't be until Week 9 at the earliest.

Even with those limitations and his potentially short-lived role, Miller's projected workload over the next few weeks makes him a strong volume-based flex play for desperate managers seeking to patch a lineup hole.

Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (29 Percent Rostered)

Coleman was a marquee waiver target in the wake of a breakout Week 2 performance, but wound up landing on the IR just days later due to a high-ankle sprain. Now that he's finally eligible to return, the Broncos RB could be a sneaky strong addition on the Week 7 waiver wire.

Denver desperately needs a playmaker to emerge after its bottom-10 offense mustered a pitiful 168 yards this past week. The team is averaging fewer than 85 yards per game on the ground this season and hasn't been able to get anything consistent going with the tandem of J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey leading the backfield.

Expect Coleman to get ample opportunity to energize this rushing attack if he returns against the Arizona Cardinals as expected. Coleman amassed a respectable 58 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries against a historically strong Jacksonville Jaguars opponent in his last appearance and could feast against a much-weaker Arizona front.

Samaje Perine, Cincinnati Bengals (5 Percent Rostered)

Chase Brown managers have reason for concern after Perine's performance in Week 5. He helped compensate for Brown's lackluster production and could see an expanded role when Cincinnati returns from its Week 6 bye.

Perine was the most effective Bengals running back during the team's most recent outing, turning his 14 carries into 68 yards while adding 10 yards and a score on two receptions. Brown saw an equal number of touches in that 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins, but only gained 60 yards in total and failed to find pay dirt.

It remains to be seen if Cincinnati will continue to divvy up the touches equally between the two backs, but Perine should be rostered and even deserves some flex consideration in Week 7 due to his upside in a timeshare.

Tyrone Tracy Jr., New York Giants (4 Percent Rostered)

The G-Men shocked the fantasy world with their soft benching of Cam Skattebo in Sunday's clash against the New Orleans Saints.

With the star sophomore seeing action on just six offensive plays (a 7.8 percent offensive snap share that was far below the 64.6 percent he was averaging over the first five weeks) and failing to log a single touch, a path was cleared for Tracy's return to prominence.

Tracy seized the opportunity, finishing a 34-27 loss with 18 rushing yards plus a touchdown on six totes and catching two of his three targets for 27 receiving yards and another score.

While Tracy's 18.5-point fantasy day was inefficient and largely buoyed by a pair of TDs, he's still worth deploying while Skattebo is stuck in head coach John Harbaugh's doghouse.

Don't invest too heavily here, though, as Skattebo returning to his usual role would quickly render Tracy—who had just seven carries over the first five weeks—irrelevant for fantasy purposes.

Germie Bernard, Pittsburgh Steelers (50 Percent Rostered)

Bernard was a trendy waiver pickup at this time last week thanks to a promising Week 5 performance, but Sunday's 25.7-point explosion makes him a must-add in just about every format he's still available in.

The rookie cemented his status as Pittsburgh's top wideout during an 11-catch, 87-receiving yard, one-touchdown Week 6 performance. He even reeled in the game-winning score in overtime, showing he's fully earned the trust of quarterback Aaron Rodgers and won't shrink from the spotlight.

After racking up 20 targets and 40.1 fantasy points over the past two weeks, Bernard should be considered a low-end WR2 for his Week 7 bout against the New Orleans Saints.

While he'll be out on bye the following week, the rookie will be a big contributor for the remainder of the season and should be your top priority waiver target if you need any help whatsoever at the WR position.

Jordyn Tyson, New Orleans Saints (49 Percent Rostered)

This is the last call on Tyson, who is still available in just over half of all leagues despite his sky-high ceiling and potential to return as early as Week 7.

Saints head coach Kellen Moore revealed that Tyson made the trip to Paris on Monday morning, setting the stage for a possible debut against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

While only truly desperate managers will want to roll the dice on Tyson making a fantasy impact this week, he's the perfect stash candidate for those who can free up a bench spot for the next couple weeks. Once he's through his Week 8 bye, Tyson's talent and upside in a high-octane New Orleans offensive system should make the No. 8 overall pick a plug-and-play WR3 with WR2 potential for the remainder of the campaign.

Keenan Allen, Indianapolis Colts (47 Percent Rostered)

Allen has turned back the clock during his brief stint in Indianapolis. The 34-year-old has garnered at least five targets in all five games he's been active for and continues to gain steam as the season wears on.

A groin injury kept him out in Week 4, but Allen is firmly back on the fantasy radar after generating 20 targets over the last two weeks and achieving season highs with eight receptions and 82 receiving yards during Sunday's loss to the Tennessee Titans.

While some of this increased production can be attributed to the absence of star tight end Tyler Warren, Allen has emerged as Indy's most trustworthy wideout and a clear favorite for QB Daniel Jones to target.

As one of the few consistent contributors in Indianapolis' offense, Allen should remain fantasy-relevant—especially if deep threat Alec Pierce continues to miss time with his heel injury.

With Allen's rostership approaching 50 percent, managers looking for a reliable receiver should consider adding him before his availability shrinks further.

Omar Cooper Jr., New York Jets (4 Percent Rostered)

Cooper's rookie campaign hit a snag when he picked up a high-ankle sprain in the opener, but he made his triumphant return from a four-week IR stint on Sunday. The Indiana product hit the ground running and consistently flashed the elite talent that led Gang Green to draft him in the first round.

Cooper exploded for 103 yards and a touchdown on six catches, adding some much-needed punch to a passing game that had stagnated without him. The 22-year-old led New York in targets, receptions and receiving yardage during a 26-19 defeat to the New England Patriots.

While he still needs to prove he can perform at this level on a consistent basis before fantasy managers can trust him as a reliable starter, Cooper has flex appeal for the Jets' upcoming clash with the Miami Dolphins.

Hunter Henry, New England Patriots (52 Percent Rostered)

Although Henry started off the 2026 campaign on a low note, his reestablished chemistry with quarterback Drake Maye is resulting in steady TE1-tier numbers.

By hauling in four of his five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets, Henry has now tallied double-digit fantasy point totals in three consecutive weeks and scored in back-to-back contests.

Even with A.J. Brown returning to the lineup and commanding a team-high 10 targets in Week 6, the veteran tight end still managed to achieve a respectable fantasy line—one that indicates he can continue producing at that level for the remainder of the season.

Henry hasn't finished worse than the TE16 since Week 3 and has a bright Week 7 outlook against a Chicago Bears defense that just got torched for two touchdowns by Kyle Pitts. Whether you need a one-week rental or a long-term starter, Henry is the best choice on waivers right now.

T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings (31 Percent Rostered)

Hockenson is one of the more intriguing tight ends you can scoop off waivers in Week 7.

The Vikings' veteran hasn't had a real opportunity to build on the explosive 24.9-point outing he put together in Week 4. Hockenson's TE1 momentum was stalled by a concussion suffered less than a minute into a Week 5 tilt against the New Orleans Saints, the final game before Minnesota's bye.

With Hockenson benefitting from an extra week to heal up, he should come out of the break strong against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy hasn't done well against tight ends recently—most notably allowing Pat Freiermuth to ring up a pair of touchdowns in Week 5—and will struggle to contain Hockenson if he rekindles the form he displayed when he was last healthy.

Michael Mayer, Las Vegas Raiders (8 Percent Rostered)

Backup tight ends rarely generate anywhere close to the type of target volume required to be fantasy relevant, but Mayer is bucking the trend in 2026. He's well behind superstar Brock Bowers in the Raiders' hierarchy, but Mayer has emerged as a viable waiver target at a position largely bereft of consistent contributors.

Mayer is coming off his best game of the campaign, tallying 16.5 fantasy points and recording his second top-10 finish of the past three weeks. Vegas' potent tight end tandem each generated nine targets in Week 6, but Mayer's 7/95/0 line outshined the starter's 4/70/0 performance.

Although he doesn't have a high ceiling, Mayer has established a safe floor by finishing as the TE25 or better in five out of six contests in 2026. He's breached double-digits in fantasy points in three of his last four games, a string that could easily continue when the Raiders face the reeling Los Angeles Rams in Week 7.

articles.title: Commanders' Dan Quinn appears to lose track of downs one week after clock debacle – but he has an explanation
articles.summary: Dan Quinn's apparent gaffe on Monday Night Football sparked game management blame on ESPN but coach explained what really happened after the game.
articles.body: Dan Quinn has a public relations problem right now and at the heart of the issue is some powerful people that are painting him as something of an NFL sideline bungler as the Washington Commanders coach. That's exactly how he looked in the second quarter of the Monday Night Football game where his team rallied to lose against the San Francisco 49ers. The problem? Quinn seemed to lose track of the downs in a key second-quarter situation. He seemed to think it was fourth down and called for a field goal when, in fact, his offense had just run a fourth-down play and, not only didn't convert, but also drew a penalty. NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 5 HAD THE COMMANDERS TAKING A TIE MORE OFFENSIVE THAN REDSKINS NICKNAME EVER WAS So, there was the coach on national television, seemingly calling for his field goal unit to get on the field when his offense had surrendered the football. And we interrupt this coaching nightmare to say Quinn contends that's not what happened at all. He told reporters a much different version of events after the game. "No, I definitely knew it was fourth down," the coach said. "We were going for it, and I was, I think with whatever you're referring to, I think it was the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. "Like, it's the turnover on downs. Like, I think somebody asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?' ... I knew what happened. I think I was probably just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me after an illegal shift, um, like, it was a turnover on downs." That's an explanation most of the country missed because it happened in Quinn's postgame press conference which wasn't nationally televised. What many instead will remember was what they saw on TV, which made the coach look bad. So, if perception is reality, Quinn is going to have to rehabilitate his increasingly tarnished reputation as a sideline game manager. That's because just last week, Quinn's Commanders utterly embarrassed themselves in how they managed a last-minute situation against the New York Giants, wasting precious seconds, mismanaging the clock and the downs, and settling for a tie when they should have likely won the game. NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 2 GOES TO JETS COACH AARON GLENN WHO PLAYED NOT TO LOSE AT END OF REGULATION That terrible scenario that doesn't easily fade definitely caused everyone to believe Quinn was at it again on Monday night – messing up again, forgetting that the last play was fourth down instead of third down. "Field goal," Quinn seemingly said as ABC's cameras caught him and lip readers across the world did their thing. And then he followed with, "Oh, that was fourth down." That scene not only played out during the game, but was then discussed at halftime on both the ESPN main broadcast and the Pat McAfee alternate broadcast. "We found out at halftime Dan Quinn didn't know what down it was," McAfee told his audience. "That's a real problem." The McAfee crew that featured Dan Orlovsky had some fun with the issue because the former quarterback was yelling for Quinn to kick a field goal on fourth down instead of going for it. Quinn, they joked, wanted to kick the field goal Orlovsky wanted on fifth down. "Dan Quinn did not know it's fourth down coming off of last week, and then to go for it and get the penalty," Orlovsky said. "I'm a Dan Quinn guy. But you gotta get the operation better." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This leaves Quinn in a rough spot. He's probably going to have to explain what happened to Commanders' owner Josh Harris because last week opened the door to everyone believing the coach is indeed capable of making a boneheaded mistake. The question now is whether everyone, including Harris, believes Quinn's explanation or they believe the lip-readers more. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: ‘Fake Tony Soprano’ – Eagles urged to fire Howie Roseman by former NFL player
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts’ developing injury situation is causing a lot of concern across the nation as the Philadelphia Eagles’ quarterback looks set to miss the remainde...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts' developing injury situation is causing a lot of concern across the nation as the Philadelphia Eagles' quarterback looks set to miss the remainder of the season.

Many find themselves asking how Hurts was put at such risk by those at the very top of the Eagles' organisation. The health issue is not just impacting Hurts' ability to play football but there are also wider health issues he's facing as a result.

"Again, I'm not a medical expert. Same deal there. We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation. That's where we were," Nick Sirianni said on Monday.

However, the reasoning is not going down well with people on the outside as Hurts was seemingly placed at risk after being allowed to fly back to the United States following the game in London. Former NFL nose tackle Breiden Fehoko has spoken publicly on his X account to criticise the organisation for allowing this to all unfold.

Howie Roseman told to walk after Eagles suffer huge Jalen Hurts blow

Over the years, Roseman has been widely praised for his work as the general manager of the Philadelphia Eagles . This is certainly not his finest hour and he is definitely being held accountable by former players and fans alike.

"Howie Roseman needs to be fired. Fire that fake Tony soprano stunt double. Fire everyone involved with this organisation. You knew he had a blood clot, told him not to sleep and then cleared him to PLAY! F*** the NFL," Fehoko said on X .

Roseman has pulled off some impressive acquisitions for the Eagles in the past but the organisation has failed at the basic level of care for their players in this instance. It is the fact that Hurts' issue was seemingly apparent following medical checks and he was still cleared to fly home that is concerning people outside of the team.

There is a feeling that someone needs to be held accountable for putting the team's star player at such a risk and clearly Roseman is being named as that guy. Given the severity of the issue, the Eagles' end to the season will be the last thing on the mind for a lot of people after Hurts' health has been placed under such risk.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City believing again as the Chiefs make their case for another Super Bowl appearance
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have won five straight games to open the 2026 season, putting them back in the Super Bowl conversation after missing the playoffs
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs have won five straight games to open the 2026 season, putting them back in the Super Bowl conversation after missing the playoffs last year. Their 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday offered another sign that this team is finding its rhythm. Patrick Mahomes threw for 272 yards, while Kenneth Walker III powered the ground game with 128 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The early results are encouraging, but the bigger change is how Kansas City is winning. Mahomes has more help, and the defense is giving the Chiefs another reason to believe.Patrick Mahomes has a more balanced offense around himMahomes remains the player who can change a game in a few possessions, but Kansas City's offense is no longer built around the need for him to do everything. Walker has given the Chiefs a reliable running option, forcing opposing defenses to account for more than the quarterback's arm.His performance against the Chargers showed why that matters. Walker rushed for 128 yards and two touchdowns, helping Kansas City control the game without asking Mahomes to carry every drive through the air. That balance can make life harder for defensive coordinators, who must decide whether to commit extra players to stopping the run or leave more room for Mahomes to attack downfield.For the Chiefs, this is a useful change from an offense that can sometimes become too dependent on its star quarterback. Mahomes still sets the standard, and his 272 passing yards against Los Angeles showed that the passing game remains productive. But when the running attack can take over stretches of a game, Kansas City has another way to win.That could become especially valuable against playoff teams capable of putting pressure on Mahomes and limiting his chances to make big plays.The defense is giving Kansas City another edgeKansas City's defensive performance against the Chargers was just as important as the offensive numbers. Allowing only six points gave the Chiefs room to manage the game, rather than chase the scoreboard or rely on a late comeback.That kind of control will matter against stronger opponents. In the postseason, even a productive offense can struggle when facing elite quarterbacks, tight coverage and pressure at the line. A defense that can limit scoring and give Mahomes more chances to work with a lead would make Kansas City a tougher matchup.Head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo also bring years of experience preparing for high-stakes games. Their ability to adjust to different offensive styles could prove important when the Chiefs face teams with more firepower than the Chargers showed on Sunday.Still, one strong defensive outing does not settle every question. Kansas City will need to show that it can maintain this level against a wider range of opponents before its defense becomes a clear postseason advantage.Another Super Bowl run is within reach, but work remainsThe Chiefs have made a convincing start, yet five wins do not guarantee a deep playoff run. Injuries, tougher opponents and mistakes in close games can quickly change a team's outlook. Kansas City must keep Mahomes healthy, preserve its offensive balance and show that the defense can deliver consistently.The encouraging sign is that the Chiefs do not appear to need a perfect performance from Mahomes to win. Walker's emergence gives the offense another identity, while the defense has helped keep games under control. That combination gives Kansas City a stronger foundation than a team relying on passing production alone.After missing the playoffs last season, the Chiefs have given their supporters a reason to think bigger again. Their undefeated start does not make a Super Bowl appearance inevitable, but it has changed the conversation. articles.title: Terry McLaurin believed to have season-ending knee injury
articles.summary: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conj...
articles.body:
Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin had to be carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee on Monday night and the image didn't do much to conjure up hopes of a quick return to the field this season.

Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that the team feared a "significant" injury after the game and that McLaurin would go for tests on Tuesday to determine just how significant it is. Those tests are pending, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the team is bracing to learn that McLaurin will miss the rest of the season.

McLaurin missed Week 4 with a hamstring injury and has 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown on the season.

McLaurin has two more years left on his contract and is set to have a $34 million cap number in 2027, but there's no guaranteed money left on the deal should the Commanders opt to move in a different direction.

The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and reportedly ready to be aggressive at the trade deadline. Who should they target? That's the question driving the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, where host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano fired up the brand-new A to Z Sports Trade Simulator to break down every realistic target — from DeForest Buckner to Saquon Barkley to Cam Bynum.

"If the Vikings want to truly make a Super Bowl run they should make a couple of trades and fortify the roster," Forness said, pointing to past champions like the 2021 Rams adding Odell Beckham Jr. and the Seahawks acquiring Rashid Shaheed as proof that late-season additions matter. GM Nolan Teasley comes from an aggressive organization and has been calling around. "We've heard Nolan Teasley's calling around," Forness noted. "All the beat reporters like the Vikings are going to add people."

DeForest Buckner is the #1 target. "I think the number one player I wanna bring in of anybody that I think could realistically be available is DeForest Buckner," Forness said. Beyond the playoff push, he sees Buckner as a developmental mentor for rookie Caleb Banks due to their similar builds (6'6″+, 34-35″ arms) and leverage techniques. Likely cost: a third-round pick plus a token sixth.

Justin Herbert doesn't fit. Despite tantalizing arm talent, Forness has major concerns: "I have concerns that he doesn't fit this offense." He questioned whether three first-round picks is worth it for a QB thriving in Sean Payton/Joe Lombardi systems, not Kevin O'Connell's anticipatory West Coast offense.

Quenton Nelson is a risky rental. Stefano noted Nelson is "the fourth-ranked guard in PFF right now" and "a Pro Bowl guard," but Forness pushed back on spending two thirds for a 30-year-old rental when Donovan Jackson is expected back for the playoffs.

Jonathan Taylor carries too much tread. With 2,599 carries since college vs. Jordan Mason's 859, Forness cautioned: "Tread on the tires matters with running backs. It, we don't want it to, but it does." Likely cost: a second-round pick.

Cam Bynum reunion makes sense. With Theo Jackson struggling, Forness explained: "This is a PhD level defense where rookies don't often get a lot of playing time." Bynum already knows Brian Flores' system, eliminating the learning curve. Proposed deal: a third, a fifth, and Theo Jackson for Bynum and a fourth.

Saquon Barkley is within reach. A third-round pick plus a fifth could land the Eagles star, creating a devastating trio with Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

Pass rush is the priority. "Pass rush, defensive line, I think that should be the priority," Forness said, noting Jalen Redmond, Andrew Van Ginkel, and Dallas Turner are all playing 80-90% of snaps.

Kevin O'Connell isn't going anywhere. "You are not going to find better as a head coach if you fire him," Forness said bluntly.

Whether it's Buckner anchoring the defensive line, Bynum steadying the secondary, or a surprise running back addition, the Vikings have the capital and urgency to make a Super Bowl push.
