articles.title: The 11 Biggest Overreactions After NFL Week 6
articles.summary: Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season provided plenty for fans to chew on as the midpoint of the campaign draws closer.
articles.body:
Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season provided plenty for fans to chew on as the midpoint of the campaign draws closer.

A mix of improbable results—such as the lowly Arizona Cardinals toppling the Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams, the Tennessee Titans getting in the win column and the Cleveland Browns taking control of the AFC North—and expected outcomes (like the New England Patriots besting the New York Jets for the 19th time in 21 tries) has set the stage for a series of hot takes.

While some of these ideas have merit, many are just kneejerk responses to the scores and storylines that played out over the weekend. With that in mind, let's highlight the top 10 overreactions from Week 6.

The Buffalo Bills Can Win Without Fixing Their Defense

The Buffalo Bills rode another massive outing from Josh Allen to victory in Week 6. While the 33-30 win against the Las Vegas Raiders moved Buffalo to 5-1, the contest further revealed the cracks in the armor of the AFC East leaders.

The Bills are heavily relying on their MVP candidate quarterback to bail out an abysmal defense, one that must get fixed before the trade deadline if this franchise is going to finally break through and win a Super Bowl. The Bills are an utter mess on that side of the football, conceding an average of 386.8 yards and 28.5 points per game to opposing offenses.

Only a handful of teams have lifted a Lombardi Trophy in the modern era without the help of a top-10 defense and none have done so while being hamstrung by a bottom-five unit. The Bills cannot continue to lean on Allen and the offense to shoulder the burden of winning, as the plan will ultimately fail in spectacular fashion at some point during the playoffs.

It took Buffalo scoring on seven of nine offensive drives to get past a plucky Raiders team in the midst of a rebuild. That won't be sustainable come January when the competition gets much tougher and the stakes are far higher. The Bills need to make some drastic moves before the trade deadline to dial this defense in if they are serious about a championship.

The Cleveland Browns are the AFC North's Team to Beat

The Cleveland Browns are one of the biggest surprises of the NFL season's first six weeks, jumping out to a wildly unexpected 4-2 record and share of the AFC North lead in that span. While the Browns' surge is a nice story, they still aren't the team to beat in this incredibly tough division.

The AFC North is collectively punching up in 2026. Three of its four teams are sitting at 4-2 heading into Week 7, while the Cincinnati Bengals remain at 3-2 due to a Week 6 bye. Cleveland does have the inside track to win the divisional crown as the lone squad still unbeaten in AFC North play.

Both of Cleveland's divisional wins came by narrow three-point margins, with a 13-10 victory over Baltimore in Week 6 notably occurring against backup quarterback Tyler Huntley while Lamar Jackson was sidelined with injury. While the win still counts the same in the standings, a late season rematch could go far differently if Baltimore's superstar signal-caller is active.

The Browns still must prove they have the firepower to continue winning with regularity over the next three months. A defense that has only allowed 20.3 points per game and held three of its last four foes to 18 points or less is doing some heavy lifting, but averaging just 267.5 yards and 17.7 points (both bottom-five marks in the league) on the other end isn't going to cut it over the long term.

Cleveland has been a much tougher out than most expected going into the new season, but there is far more work to be done if this franchise is going to buck its status as perennial losers and seriously compete for its first divisional title since 1989.

The Dallas Cowboys are one of the more disappointing teams of the 2026 season. If not for the furious comeback they mounted in Week 3 against the Houston Texans, the team would be sitting at 1-5 and almost entirely out of contention before November. Although 2-4 isn't much better for a club that has Super Bowl aspirations, there is still reason to believe this franchise can turn it around.

A 23-13 defeat to the Green Bay Packers in primetime on the heels of a 24-16 loss to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad led by an undrafted rookie quarterback certainly doesn't inspire much confidence in the Cowboys, but the offense has the pieces in place to return to its early-season form. Prior to Week 5, Dallas was averaging over 30 points per game and still has all its key personnel on that side of the ball healthy.

Although it hasn't resulted in wins, the defense has shown some signs of life after a brutal opening month. The Cowboys conceded an average of 28 points over the first four games, a number that has dropped to 23.5 during the last two.

If Dallas can regularly perform at even a league-average level on defense, the offense should be strong enough to win a large portion of the team's remaining games.

Favorable scheduling will work in the Cowboys' favor, with the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, inconsistent Arizona Cardinals and reeling Indianapolis Colts representing their next three opponents. A three-game winning streak would not only have Dallas sitting back above .500, but also provide the squad the momentum it needs to make a run in the wide-open NFC East.

The Houston Texans are Back in the Playoff Hunt

The Houston Texans raised eyebrows when they elected to part with valuable draft capital in exchange for underperforming wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. last week. The trade signified that Houston intends to contend rather than throw in the towel after a 1-4 start.

The move seems to have helped in the short-term, as Harrison contributed three catches for 34 yards during his new team's much-needed 34-31 victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Despite the key Week 6 "W", it's not time to pencil Houston in for a spot on the 2027 NFL playoff bracket.

There is still much to be done before the Texans can be considered a true threat. While quarterback C.J. Stroud has been playing rather well after his postseason meltdown 10 months ago, the rushing attack remains a disaster and could be the offense's Achilles heel in 2026.

Houston's defense is also a concern despite the unit rating as one of the league's best last year. The Texans have conceded 30-plus points in half their games this season and just came close to blowing a double-digit fourth quarter lead for the second time in three weeks.

These are issues that the arrival of MHJ won't patch over. Houston should have the tools on-hand to fix these problems, but the squad can't afford any more missteps. A recent win over an AFC South rival helps, but the Texans shouldn't be considered a serious contender unless they string together some wins following their Week 8 bye.

The Indianapolis Colts Should Fire Shane Steichen Too

The Indianapolis Colts executed the first major personnel firing of the 2026 NFL season when they relieved longtime general manager Chris Ballard of his duties on Monday. The decision came on the heels of a dismal 2-4 start, continuing the string of poor play that began in the back half of the 2025 campaign.

While Ballard's inability to improve a team that began last season with an 8-2 record and ended it at 8-9—becoming the first team in NFL history to go six games above .500 and miss the playoffs—ultimately led to his dismissal, the Colts don't need to completely clean house at this time.

Head coach Shane Steichen was already on shaky ground after failing to spark Indy to a playoff appearance in any of his three previous seasons, but should get an opportunity to finish out the 2026 campaign. The Colts lack a proven in-house replacement who could step into the interim job and find immediate success. The franchise also significantly struggled the last time it attempted to place someone inexperienced in the role.

Jeff Saturday was the most recent interim head coach in Indianapolis. The former All-Pro Colts center was working at ESPN prior to accepting the gig and had no coaching experience outside of the high school ranks. Although he won his first game after replacing Frank Reich, Saturday's squad went on to lose seven straight. The interim coach was mercifully replaced by Steichen once the 2022 campaign concluded.

Although Steichen has his work cut out attempting to right this ship, the best option is letting him see it through and bringing in an entire new regime this offseason if things don't work out.

J.J. McCarthy Can Revive the New York Giants' Offense

The New York Giants' hopes of contending for a championship took a massive hit when Jaxson Dart went down for the season with an ACL tear in Week 2. While the club went 2-0-1 over the next three games with backup Jameis Winston at the reins, the cracks began to show in Week 6.

With New York's offense looking anemic against the New Orleans Saints, head coach John Harbaugh made the drastic decision to bench Winston and insert J.J. McCarthy for the fourth quarter. Although the bold move sparked three consecutive scoring drives and put Big Blue within striking distance of tying the game before the comeback bid ultimately fell short, McCarthy isn't the answer to their offensive woes.

Seeing McCarthy on the field during a meaningful contest less than a month after he joined the team shows just how desperate the G-Men are. With Winston reverting to his turnover-prone ways—tossing a pair of picks that effectively put the game out of reach—the coaching staff elected to see what it had in the third-year backup.

Although McCarthy racked up 243 passing yards in short order, he also struggled with accuracy (completing just 11 of 21 passes) and turnovers (tossing an interception on his first drive). Those same issues doomed McCarthy's chances of leading the Minnesota Vikings and will prevent him from becoming a quality starter in the Big Apple.

If McCarthy does usurp Winston as the starter going forward, the G-Men will remain a fringe playoff team at best with no real shot at contending for anything beyond a Wild Card appearance.

The Kansas City Chiefs are Unstoppable Again

The Kansas City Chiefs soundly thrashed the Los Angeles Chargers this weekend, keeping their unblemished record intact as they march towards a 10th playoff berth in 11 seasons. While it was a solid performance, the Chiefs have yet to be truly tested in 2026.

Kansas City's 22-6 victory over the Chargers didn't reveal anything new about the club. The Bolts are a bad football team that have issues across the roster, schematic concerns and injury woes that led them to start four rookie offensive linemen in Week 6. The Chiefs played smart against their imploding foe, riding another big performance from key offseason acquisition Kenneth Walker III to an easy win.

While Walker has been a revelation and has immensely helped Patrick Mahomes ease back into action after recovering from an ACL tear, the Chiefs have yet to face a legitimate Super Bowl contender this season. The combined record of their first five opponents is 9-17, with the Chargers and Miami Dolphins both winless and the Denver Broncos (who have a myriad of offensive issues to figure out) being the lone team above .500 going into Week 7.

At this rate, the Chiefs may not be challenged until well into the back half of the campaign. Their next five games are against the Seattle Seahawks, Broncos, New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals—a stretch that Kansas City is likely to be heavily favored throughout.

Things will get much tougher starting in Week 12 when the Chiefs head to Highmark Stadium to face the Buffalo Bills, kicking off a five-week stretch against multiple Super Bowl hopefuls. This includes meetings with the Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati Bengals, New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers in consecutive weeks.

If the Chiefs can get through that portion of the schedule with a winning record and remain in the AFC's driver's seat, then it will be time to seriously consider them a Lombardi Trophy threat. Until then, they remain a team that still has to prove last year's 6-11 finish was a fluke.

The Los Angeles Rams Are No Longer a Super Bowl Threat

The Los Angeles Rams' 2-4 start is arguably the biggest shock of the 2026 NFL season. The team was a heavy Super Bowl favorite coming into the campaign, but a series of injuries and poor on-field performances has set the team back significantly in the weeks since.

Los Angeles hit a new low during an 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, a stunning loss that has many rightfully questioning whether this group can still win it all.

While the Rams will now try to become the first team to overcome a losing record through six weeks and still reach the Super Bowl, this team does boast the collective talent to make history.

L.A. still has the reigning MVP under center in Matt Stafford. At the age of 38 and in his 18th NFL season, the veteran signal-caller is the type of steady handy that an underperforming squad needs to dig itself out of a rut. Stafford has experienced all the highs and lows the league can offer and has the experience needed to right the ship. His chemistry with Puka Nacua will help offset the absence of Davante Adams, who could be out two-plus months after rupturing a hamstring.

Even without reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in the picture, the Rams have collected enough talent on that side of the ball to lock down opponents. They rank top-five in total and passing defense and will only get better once Garrett returns from the knee surgery that has kept him sidelined since the opener.

Special teams remains the most concerning issue the Rams are dealing with. The team made the drastic decision to release kicker Brandon Mevis and sign Blake Grupe, but the decision backfired after Grupe was injured in his first game. If L.A. can find a stable kicker and clean up its coverage, there should be a rapid and noticeable improvement in the team's overall performance.

With their backs against the wall and a soft schedule upcoming, the Rams should be able to rip off a winning streak that will bring them above .500 and right back into the Super Bowl discussion before the calendar flips to December.

The New England Patriots Made a Mistake Trading for A.J. Brown

The New England Patriots' trade with the Philadelphia Eagles for A.J. Brown was one of the splashiest moves of the 2026 NFL offseason, but thus far the deal hasn't panned out as expected.

Brown was supposed to represent an upgrade over Stefon Diggs, the incumbent No. 1 wideout who New England released following a successful one-year stint with the franchise.

That hasn't come to fruition, as Brown followed up a three-catch, 26-receiving yard performance in his New England debut with a monthlong stint on the IR. His Week 6 return from a high-ankle sprain was anything but triumphant, as the veteran wideout caught just three of his team-high 10 targets and gained a mere 27 yards.

Despite the slow start, it's too early to consider New England's trade a blunder.

Brown is a three-time Pro Bowler who eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards in six of his first seven NFL seasons. Even last year when he was clearly disgruntled with his role in Philly's offense, Brown still contributed 1,003 receiving yards and seven touchdowns on 78 catches.

Brown's production should spike up rapidly once he's recovered fully from the ankle sprain and builds a rapport with star quarterback Drake Maye. It may take a few more weeks to find his rhythm, but it would be a genuine shock if the receiver isn't playing a starring role in the offense come playoff time.

The New Orleans Saints Are Back on Track

The Saints had some sleeper playoff potential heading into the 2026 season, but a 1-4 start tempered expectations around this upstart program. The team did manage to snap a three-game losing skid and secure its second win of the campaign on Sunday, but that 34-27 victory over the New York Giants doesn't prove New Orleans is truly back on track.

The Saints had to overcome a slow start, falling into an early 10-0 hole before waking up and putting 34 answered points on the board. Despite chasing Giants starting quarterback Jameis Winston from the game at the start of the fourth quarter, New Orleans nearly squandered its 24-point lead to a J.J. McCarthy-led foe and needed a fourth down stop in the end zone to avoid a potential overtime.

While the upside of head coach Kellen Moore's high-powered offensive system was on display at times, quarterback Tyler Shough still plenty of room to improve after completing a meager 53.3 percent of his throws for 144 yards in the contest. A ground game that put up a collective 175 yards on 38 totes was promising to see, but this unit has largely underwhelmed in 2026 and still needs to show it can establish the run with regularity.

It wasn't the type of start or finish that inspires confidence in this group, especially ahead of a trip to Paris to face a tough Pittsburgh Steelers team in Week 7. It won't be safe to say the team is back on track unless it enters a Week 8 bye with a 3-4 record and momentum.

The Philadelphia Eagles' 2026 season hasn't gone to plan. The team was seeking to bounce back from an unsuccessful Super Bowl title defense and return to the upper echelon of contenders, but a rash of injuries, questionable trades and poor play has led the franchise to stumble to a 2-4 record out of the gate.

While the Eagles lost their fourth straight game on Sunday and will be without Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the campaign after blood clots were found in the quarterback's lungs, there is still ample opportunity for this franchise to reach the playoffs.

In most other divisions it would be time to give up on the campaign, but Philadelphia benefits heavily from playing in a wide-open NFC East that has no clear frontrunner after six weeks of play.

The New York Giants are currently leading the pack with a modest 3-2-1 record. Despite this, the G-Men were forced to play recently-acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy in an effort to get their listless offense going. The Dallas Cowboys have scored 30 total points over the past two weeks and lost three of their last four, joining the Eagles at 2-4 with their latest defeat. The Washington Commanders have issues across the roster and are facing an uphill battle to recover from their 1-4-1 start.

If the Eagles can stabilize their offense under promising backup Tanner McKee, there is a chance they can string together some wins and jump out as the top team in a weak division. Philly fans know better than most that backups have sparked Super Bowl runs before, including in 2017 when Nick Foles led the Eagles to their first ever Lombardi Trophy after taking over for an injured Carson Wentz.

The odds of that type of run occurring again may look bleak, but the Eagles shouldn't be counted out yet. They'll get a chance to turn things around and build some momentum when they host the Cowboys in a pivotal Week 7 showdown.

articles.title: 4 biggest disappointments in NFL after Week 6
articles.summary: 4 of the biggest NFL disappointments after 6 weeks of the 2026-27 NFL season.
articles.body:
The NFL has been entertaining to watch through the first six weeks, but some disappointing trends deserve more discussion. What is going on in Los Angeles with the Chargers and Rams? Was the NFC East hype dragged out too far? Is Cam Ward a draft bust? Let's dive in!

The Los Angeles Rams in the offseason; many fans were already gifting them the Super Bowl in August. Now, the team has their backs against the wall with a 2-4 record. They are still a poor special-teams team, but their offense is strong. Their defense is towards the middle of the pack in terms of total EPA.

Where does the team go from here? The Rams need to find ways to win these close battles. Matthew Stafford and this offense need to come together and start dominating teams. This team should be violent, but losing to the Arizona Cardinals is a tough look on the 2026 season resume.

Cam Ward was expected to take a jump with the Titans, bringing over Brian Daboll to be their offensive coordinator, drafting Carnell Tate, and adding former Giants WR Wandale Robinson. The team is averaging 14.9 points per game, and it doesn't seem like this team is going to improve.

The offense is ranked 30th in EPA/Play, and they are 29th in EPA/Pass. Does this team find a way to tank for Jerimaeh Smith from Ohio State?

The Chargers' offense was getting lots of hype with the addition of Mike McDaniel joining the staff to be their offensive coordinator. Justin Herbert has not looked great, and now the team is considering pivoting to Adam Gase as their new guy. Omarion Hampton was getting some hype because Mike McDaniel is very good with running backs.

Jim Harbaugh's seat is getting hotter and hotter. The team's schedule is one of the toughest in the NFL, and if they continue to lose, then the Chargers are going to have to consider deciding on a new coach. This is the first time they started 0-6 since 2000, and their quarterback was Jim Harbaugh.

The NFC East are winless in the last two weeks, and this season is going downhill quickly. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with a blood clot; the Commanders have issues with Dan Quinn, and their team can't stay healthy; the Cowboys' defense has lots of money invested, and they still can't get stops. The Giants continue to have issues with their quarterback situation. They need to figure out how to stop the run too.

There is a good chance that Dan Quinn (WAS), Nick Sirianni (PHI), and Brian Schotenhiemer (DAL) could all be out of jobs even before the end of the season.

articles.summary: ericbvd/Depositphotos Why NFL teams struggle to build balanced rosters NFL teams often invest heavily in star players, but individual talent cannot solve eve...
articles.body:
Why NFL teams struggle to build balanced rosters

NFL teams often invest heavily in star players, but individual talent cannot solve every problem on a roster. Offensive-line protection, defensive depth, salary-cap limits and quarterback development all play important roles in a team's success.

Recent roster decisions involving the Detroit Lions, Houston Texans, Cleveland Browns and Dallas Cowboys highlight the challenges of building a balanced team.

Failing to protect the franchise quarterback

Quarterbacks receive major contracts and often become the center of a team's long-term plans. However, Houston's experience entering 2026 shows why quarterback investment must be matched by reliable offensive-line protection.

C.J. Stroud was sacked 90 times during his first two NFL seasons, ranking second among quarterbacks from his draft class behind Bryce Young. His sack total fell to 23 in 2025, demonstrating how changes in protection can affect a quarterback's exposure to pressure.

Treating offensive-line problems as temporary

Offensive-line weaknesses can persist across multiple seasons when teams repeatedly replace departing starters rather than build continuity. Houston continued addressing its protection problems during the 2026 offseason, while Detroit faced challenges following major personnel losses.

Detroit lost guard Kevin Zeitler in free agency and center Frank Ragnow to retirement before the 2025 season. Injuries and replacements led to frequent lineup changes, leaving the Lions with another major offensive-line priority heading into 2026.

Giving quarterbacks a stronger supporting cast

Drafting a promising quarterback does not automatically solve a franchise's offensive problems. Young passers also benefit from effective protection, dependable receivers and clear coaching.

Cleveland evaluated Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders during the 2026 offseason before naming Watson its opening-day starter on August 24. The Browns also rebuilt their offensive line through trades, free agency and the draft, showing how a quarterback decision fits into a broader effort to strengthen an offense.

Spending heavily without accounting for depth

A roster's starting lineup does not tell the full story of its readiness for a long NFL season. Injuries, substitutions and departures can force teams to rely on less experienced players at important positions.

Philadelphia entered the 2026 season with concerns about offensive line depth, including questions about players dealing with recurring injuries. NFL.com also identified depth as a concern for San Francisco's offensive line, showing that even established contenders must plan for personnel changes beyond their starting groups.

Rebuilding the same position group repeatedly

Repeatedly rebuilding a position group can leave teams struggling to establish consistency from one season to the next. Free agency, trades and draft selections offer solutions, but they also require teams to manage departures and replacements together.

The Browns faced this challenge entering 2026 after preparing for significant changes along the offensive line. NFL.com reported that Cleveland was set to lose potentially four of its five 2025 starters, creating a substantial personnel problem alongside its unresolved quarterback situation.

Neglecting the defense while building the offense

An offense filled with productive players cannot, on its own, prevent opponents from scoring. Teams must also maintain an effective pass rush, cover receivers and stop running plays to compete across a full season.

The Dallas Cowboys entered 2026 with significant defensive needs after trading Micah Parsons before the 2025 season. NFL.com identified the pass rush and secondary as areas requiring attention, illustrating how losing a major defensive contributor can create multiple roster-building challenges.

Interesting fact : The NFL's salary cap topped $301.2 million for the first time in 2026.

Building a unit takes more than one signing

A prominent signing can address a clear weakness, but dependable offensive-line play requires several players working together. Teams must consider scheme fit, communication and depth alongside individual ability.

Houston retained Ed Ingram and Trent Brown with contract extensions during the 2026 offseason and added other offensive linemen. Those moves formed part of a broader effort to protect C.J. Stroud and maintain continuity across the unit.

Ignoring how injuries affect long-term plans

Injuries can change a team's priorities even when its original roster plan appears sound. Reliable backup players and flexible personnel options help teams respond when starters miss games or struggle to return to full health.

Detroit used 13 offensive linemen during the 2025 season, tying for the league lead in that category. The number reflected the combined effects of roster changes and injuries, while highlighting the challenge of maintaining a consistent unit throughout an NFL campaign.

Matching draft investments to roster needs

The NFL Draft gives teams a chance to address weaknesses while developing players for the future. Combining draft selections with veteran additions can provide several ways to strengthen the same position group.

Detroit addressed its offensive line by selecting Clemson tackle Blake Miller with the No. 17 pick in the 2026 draft and signing center Cade Mays in free agency. The approach combined a first-round investment with the addition of an experienced professional following significant changes to the unit.

Balancing roster needs against the salary cap

NFL teams must balance immediate improvements against the financial commitments in player contracts. Spending on one position can reduce the flexibility available to strengthen another.

In a February 20, 2026, assessment, NFL.com reported that Houston was $4.7 million over its projected salary-cap limit. The Texans later extended Ed Ingram and Trent Brown, illustrating how roster planning involves both managing financial commitments and deciding which contributors to retain.

Adapting when the original lineup changes

Injuries and personnel changes can force teams to revise their plans during the season. Green Bay responded to early protection problems by adding veteran guard Laken Tomlinson and changing its starting combinations.

Through Week 3, Jordan Love had taken 31 hits, and the Packers ranked 31st in pressure rate allowed at 44.7%. Their protection improved in Weeks 4–5, when Love took 7 hits and the team allowed pressure on 20.3% of dropbacks, according to an October 15 NFL.com report.

The NFL playoff picture can change quickly as teams develop their strengths and capitalize on weaknesses across the league. Check out how these 6 NFL teams could shake up the Super Bowl race .

Repeating mistakes instead of building a complete roster

Star players give teams an advantage, but dependable protection, defensive contributors and capable reserves help keep a season on course. Building that support requires decisions across the roster, from retaining veterans to developing draft picks and responding to injuries.

Detroit's offensive-line investments, Houston's contract extensions and Green Bay's adjustments show the different ways teams can respond. The challenge continues after opening day, as front offices and coaches work to keep their personnel suited to the demands of the season.

Officials play a central role in maintaining order and enforcing rules during high-pressure NFL games, making disciplinary decisions a closely watched issue. Find out why the NFL suspended two referees after heated player incidents .

Which roster-building mistake do you think hurts NFL teams the most? Like this post and share your opinion in the comments.

articles.title: Stefon Diggs Says It's 'Wide Open' for Commanders in NFC East Despite 1-4-1 Start to NFL Season
articles.summary: On the heels of another close loss for the Washington Commanders that dropped their record to 1-4-1, Stefon Diggs believes they are still more than capable of winning the NFC East.
articles.body:
On the heels of another close loss for the Washington Commanders that dropped their record to 1-4-1, Stefon Diggs believes they are still more than capable of winning the NFC East.

Speaking to reporters after Monday's 23-17 defeat against the San Francisco 49ers, Diggs said "it's still wide open" for the Commanders in the division race.

The Commanders nearly overcame a 23-3 deficit by scoring 14 unanswered points against the 49ers. They had the ball in San Francisco territory on the final play of the game, but Jayden Daniels was sacked to end it.

This was yet another week in which the Commanders' situational awareness and late-game execution left something to be desired. Daniels threw the ball away on a fourth-and-2 early in the second quarter down 13-3.

On the second-to-last offensive possession, the Commanders had to call a timeout when it appeared as if they were late lining up out of the huddle. This allowed the 49ers to run more time off the clock on their next possession so Washington got the ball back with 52 seconds to play.

The final drive saw Daniels called for intentional grounding after the Commanders got down to the Niners' 28-yard line. The penalty not only cost them 10 yards, but an automatic 10-second runoff so there were only six seconds remaining for the final play.

Despite some of these recent issues and their current record, which has them sitting last in the division, Diggs' statement that things are still wide open feels accurate.

No team in the NFC East has won a game since Week 4. The New York Giants are the only team in the division with a winning record (3-2-1). The Dallas Cowboys (2-4) have put up 29 points in their last two games. The Philadelphia Eagles are a mess right now and won't have Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season.

Given how well Daniels is playing, even with some of situational mistakes, and the fourth-easiest remaining strength of schedule, there's no reason the Commanders can't be atop the NFC East when the regular season ends.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts’ health issue sparks accountability debate as Super Bowl champion insists Eagles cannot escape consequences
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing questions over their handling of Jalen Hurts’ health after reports revealed that the quarterback was diagnosed with a
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing questions over their handling of Jalen Hurts’ health after reports revealed that the quarterback was diagnosed with a blood clot during the team’s London trip. Super Bowl champion James Jones believes the organization must face consequences if its medical staff cleared Hurts to play despite knowing the risks. The debate has intensified following conflicting details about Hurts’ sleep before the game and the timeline of his hospital visit. Further scans later revealed blood clots in both lungs, ruling the Eagles quarterback out for the remainder of the 2026 season.James Jones demands consequences for the Eagles’ handling of HurtsSpeaking on “Pregame, A Speakeasy Show,” Jones questioned the decision to allow Hurts to play and argued that the people responsible for protecting players must be held accountable.“A punishment has to happen. You are dealing with a young man’s life that we are putting in your hands when it comes to injuries,” Jones said.The former NFL wide receiver pointed to the presence of doctors and trainers at games, saying their primary responsibility is to protect players rather than expose them to unnecessary danger.“That’s why we have trainers and doctors and all that in the stadium. There’s no organization that says, ‘If something happens, you gotta go over there.’ Everybody is in the building and hired for a reason: to protect and help the players. So, a punishment has to happen because you put this young man in harm’s way.”Jones also challenged the reported circumstances surrounding Hurts’ condition before the game. He questioned how medical professionals could approve his participation if they believed he had been awake for around 36 hours and needed to keep moving to maintain blood circulation.“If you’re telling a dude to stay up so that his blood can keep circulating for 36 hours, he [Hurts] shouldn’t be going out there. And if you’re a doctor, you know that.”His criticism puts the focus on the medical clearance process and what the team knew before Hurts took the field.Jalen Hurts’ diagnosis raises further questions about the timelineNFL insider Ian Rapoport initially reported that Hurts remained at the hospital until around 4 a.m. and did not sleep because “sleep was a risk.” However, Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, later clarified that the quarterback slept after returning from the hospital and before kickoff.Hurts was initially diagnosed with superficial vein thrombosis in London. Additional scans over the weekend then revealed blood clots in both lungs, a more serious condition identified as deep vein thrombosis with bilateral pulmonary emboli.The diagnosis will keep him out of contact football while he takes blood thinners. His agent offered a reassuring update on Monday.“Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery,” Hurts’ agent wrote in a statement on Monday. “We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners.”That outlook offers hope for Hurts’ eventual return, but it does not settle the questions surrounding his availability for the London game. articles.title: Titans Release Jordan Elliott After Confirming 'Incident at Our Team Facility'
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans announced Tuesday they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott following "an incident at our team facility."
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans announced Tuesday they released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott following "an incident at our team facility."

Elliott had appeared in five of the team's first six games. He recorded 11 combined tackles.

The 2020 third-round pick didn't appear in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Elliott signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the Titans in the offseason. He previously suited up for the Cleveland Browns and San Francisco 49ers and was a regular starter for both teams.

Tennessee didn't disclose any details surrounding the "incident," but it likely explains why Elliott was sidelined in Week 6.

Coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi might see cutting the 28-year-old as a way to reset the organization's culture.

Elliott wasn't the only notable defensive player absent against the Colts. Cornerback Alontae Taylor, who's in the first year of his $58 million contract, was also inactive.

Elliott's exit is likely to grant more snaps to second-year tackle Nazir Stackhouse. Stackhouse was on the field for just 15 defensive snaps in Week 6 and still had three tackles in the Titans' first victory.

articles.title: NFL Paris 2026: New Orleans Saints vs Pittsburgh Steelers game 'all systems go' despite riots in French capital
articles.summary: Brett Gosper, NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, discusses unrest in Paris and the future of the NFL overseas, with the league having identified 12 potential new host cities; watch New Orleans Saints vs Pittsburgh Steelers from 1pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints will serve as the designated home team when they honour their French ties against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the nation's first regular-season game at Stade de France, live on Sky Sports NFL from 1pm.

It comes after civil unrest broke out across Paris over the weekend as peaceful protests were overshadowed by masked activists and vandals turning to violence and looting.

Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, said the league is prioritising the safety of fans and the two travelling teams, but envisions no disruption to the game.

"It hasn't impacted it, but obviously we're keeping a good eye on that and we're in very constant daily contact with the French authorities on it," Gosper told Sky Sports .

"We're not seeing our events being disrupted at this point in time and we certainly don't feel the game will be disrupted. So we're all systems go on the game for this Sunday."

Saints tight end Juwan Johnson this week said some family members were undecided as to whether they would make the trip to Paris, while Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker described the scenes in France as "crazy".

"Obviously, safety of fans and players is the high priority, and we're not going to put anyone at risk in that sense, which is why the information we're getting is very important," Gosper added. "And for the moment, it's indicating that things are good for us to go into this game in the right way."

New Orleans' connection to France dates back to 1718 when the city was founded by the French as La Nouvelle-Orléans, before becoming the capital of French Louisiana in 1722. It was two French engineers who would lay out the first 66 squares of a walled village that later became the iconic French Quarter.

The city would preserve its French DNA throughout 40 years of Spanish rule, teaching in French and adopting French culture. Even today New Orleans celebrates Bastille Day in honour of its French roots.

"There's a great alignment of culture and history between the Saints hosting a game here in the French market, for sure," said Gosper. "It's something that's not gone unnoticed by the French public. At every level, they know that connection.

"It's not like you have to be a history buff in France to understand that connection. It's understood and it's great for the Saints. They're the only team at the moment operating in the global market program, for the moment that makes them the team of France or the French team.

"It definitely creates a stronger engagement with the population of France and a likelihood that many people adopt the Saints as their club. We know that fans can be fans of the NFL, but really avid, passionate fans like to choose a team, so that's the role the Saints are playing at the moment in transforming those NFL fans into loyal club fans for the Saints."

As the Saints amplify their French ties, the NFL is too tasked with translating a French Quarter Mardis Gras-enthused feel to the gameweek. It may not quite be Bourbon Street but NOLA is coming to town.

"We'll see lots of touches of Louisiana and the Saints in the stadium, there'll also be a lot of other ceremonial activities put on by the league to underline the fact that this is a special first game in France," said Gosper. "These games, although they look very much like NFL games and mini Super Bowls in each market, they have their own personality because of what the local fans bring to the picture.

"Melbourne's not the same as Munich, which won't be the same as Paris, which is not the same as London. They're all special for different reasons of personality that the local fans bring to these games."

The NBA has been a familiar feature to the French sporting landscape having played five regular-season games in Paris since 2020, with two more scheduled across 2027 and 2028.

It is now the turn of the NFL to test its newest market amid a record nine international games being played in 2026, Paris joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as debut host cities.

"What's good is we know that the French love all of their sports," said Gosper. "They love their rugby, they love their basketball, they love their football. There's room for the NFL as well.

"The French embrace all sports, American sports, local sports, and they get very passionate about it, and that gives us comfort and optimism for the future that we'll have here."

It arrives on the back of three straight UK games held across Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and Wembley, the latter two of which were decided by last-second field goals in two of the NFL's greatest international match-ups.

"It's been magnificent," said Gosper. "The UK games themselves have been terrific, but I would say the impact of the NFL in London over that period couldn't go unnoticed.

"We probably had more impact this year than we've had in recent years, and there'll be more of that again next year. London really does embrace the NFL."

Dublin does not feature as part of this year's international schedule after making history in 2025 when the Steelers faced the Minnesota Vikings at Croke Park, but is expected to return as a host.

"We can't announce any of our programme for next year yet, but generally speaking we don't just go and play a game in a market and not come back," said Gosper.

"There'd be optimism that sometime in the near future Dublin will be back on our radar. I guess that's the good news in a Dublin sense.

"And similarly in France, we'd love to come back here at some point. That decision's not been made either. These are markets that we're here to develop over a medium and long term, and we don't just want to play a game and disappear.

"We've looked at a number of international markets, we've determined that there's about 12 markets of high interest to us on a number of criteria. The size of sport fans within the overall population, the number of fans we've got, but also where we see potential broadcast revenues over time and commercial revenues over time. At some point our investment has to pay back, so that's an important criteria as well. We kind of know those markets that are of interest to the NFL."

Gosper added the NFL is in conversations with markets in Asia over prospective games as the league explores the task of building an audience in the face of challenging time zones.

For now, the immediate focus is Paris, where Gosper will return to a familiar stomping ground in the Stade de France following his days as chief executive of World Rugby.

"I was there when France won the World Cup in 1998. That's how long I go back," he said. "I was actually in the stadium that day and how that transformed France's idea of itself as a footballing nation.

"Obviously, there's been Rugby World Cups and Olympics there since, so some major events. It'll be fantastic to see the NFL hosting a game there as well.

"It's the missing element that the Stade de France has not done yet. Great for Stade de France's history and great for the NFL's history.

"It's very special for us all to be involved in a first like this and bringing it to a big market. This game will reverberate wider than France itself."

articles.title: Who is headlining the Super Bowl halftime show? Prediction markets lean heavily toward one artist
articles.summary: The NFL and Roc Nation have yet to officially announce next year’s Super Bowl halftime performer, but users across two of the biggest prediction markets seem to think they have a pretty good idea.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) — The NFL and Roc Nation have yet to officially announce next year’s Super Bowl halftime performer, but users across two of the biggest prediction markets seem to think they have a pretty good idea.

As of Tuesday morning, the odds posted at Kalshi and Polymarket leaned heavily toward Jay-Z as the headliner of Super Bowl LXI in Feb. 2027. Jay-Z is also the founder of Roc Nation, the entertainment company that has chosen the act for, and co-produced, the Super Bowl halftime show since 2020.

Jay-Z had a hefty lead over other potential performers. At Kalshi, the market viewed Jay-Z as having about a 91 percent chance of headlining, and the odds were even greater on Polymarket .

Other performers thought to have a (much smaller) chance at headlining included Miley Cyrus, Beyonce, Harry Styles, Post Malone and Dua Lipa, among others, according to users at both prediction markets.

It’s worth noting that prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, just like traditional stock markets, prohibit insider trading. But a few factors are likely swaying users’ predictions — including an early Tuesday report from Puck which suggested Jay-Z had selected himself as the halftime entertainment. The outlet cited “multiple” unnamed sources with the news.

Jay-Z has also never headlined a Super Bowl Halftime Show, despite his long tenure as a top-selling recording artist and the founder of the company that currently chooses the halftime entertainment.

The NFL has not yet confirmed the news, though it’s likely the league will make its announcement soon. Halftime performers for the Super Bowl have generally been announced several months before the big game in September: Bad Bunny, who headlined Super Bowl LX in 2026, was formally announced on Sept. 28, 2025, while Kendrick Lamar, who headlined Super Bowl LIX in 2025, was announced Sept. 8, 2024.

There’s no question, however, who is making the final decision, insiders have said.

“It’s a decision that Jay makes,” Jesse Collins, the co-producer of the event, told Variety in 2014. “Since we’ve been on board with that show, he’s made it every year, and it’s been amazing. He’s always picked right!”

articles.title: Najee Harris Reportedly Released by Giants Days After Cam Skattebo Had 0 Carries vs. Saints
articles.summary: The New York Giants' running back room continues to raise more questions than answers.
articles.body:
The New York Giants' running back room continues to raise more questions than answers.

After Cam Skattebo registered zero carries in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that the Giants opted to release veteran ball-carrier Najee Harris.

Harris signed with the Giants on a one-year deal in August to add some depth to a crowded backfield. He never recorded 10 or more carries in a game, but he had a season-high 52 yards in a Week 3 win over the Tennessee Titans. However, his production quickly dwindled, and he was limited to four carries and two yards in Sunday's loss against the Saints.

New York mustered just 84 rushing yards against New Orleans, with backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy leading the team with 26 yards on two carries. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. had a team-high six carries for just 18 yards and the team's lone rushing touchdown, and he also caught a touchdown pass. Devin Singletary had four carries for 14 yards.

However, the story of the game was Skattebo, who was on the field for just six snaps.

"We didn't bench Cam Skattebo. It was not by design. All those guys were taking equal reps the first half. We were trying to see who could make something happen, who could get a hot hand and earn it," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game . "Nobody's really taken the bull by the horns. You can say I don't like that, I don't like you divvying up the snaps between four backs. I can tell you I don't like it, either. One of those guys needs to step up. Someone needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys has done that yet."

It's unclear what direction the Giants are planning to go in following Harris' release, but they will have to figure things out before facing the Houston Texans in Week 7.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo's Updated Fantasy Outlook After Giants Reportedly Release Najee Harris
articles.summary: After not getting a carry in Week 6, Cam Skattebo could factor back into the New York Giants' running back plans with Najee Harris no longer in the mix.
articles.body:
After not getting a carry in Week 6, Cam Skattebo could factor back into the New York Giants' running back plans with Najee Harris no longer in the mix.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Giants are releasing Harris after he ran for two yards on four carries in Sunday's loss against the New Orleans Saints.

Skattebo is still not worth starting in fantasy at this point until Giants head coach John Harbaugh shows interest in using him again, but the depth chart in New York is at least less crowded now without Harris.

Skattebo has been among the most disappointing players in fantasy so far this season. He was drafted on average with the 36th pick in PPR leagues coming into the year.

The initial production from Skattebo was solid, as he finished top-20 in PPR points in Weeks 1 and 3. In Weeks 4 and 5, however, he put up a total of 14.7 fantasy points on 34 touches.

An overtime fumble deep in Washington Commanders territory in the 27-27 tie in Week 5 seemed to cost Skattebo his starting role the following week. He didn't start and played a total of six offensive snaps against the Saints.

Harbaugh denied after Sunday's loss that Skattebo was being punished for the fumble against Washington:

"It was not by design. I mean, all those guys were taking equal reps in the first half. We were trying to see who could make something happen, who could kinda get a hot hand and earn it. Nobody's really taking the bull by the horns... It wasn't by design for him not to carry the ball. It was just, when he was in there, we didn't call any runs."

Even though the fumble against Washington was the first Skattebo has lost this season, it was his fourth time coughing up the ball in five games. James Cook III is the only other running back with at least four fumbles so far this season.

Harris' release is unlikely to have a significant impact on Skattebo's touches because he has barely been a factor for the offense. The 28-year-old played a total of 61 snaps in five games.

The Giants had six different players get at least one carry against New Orleans. Tyrone Tracy Jr. led the group with six. No one else had more than four. Some of that can be attributed to the game script because they trailed by as many 24 points in the second half.

This week also is a bad matchup for Skattebo to try getting back on track even if he does see a bigger workload. The Giants will take on the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium.

The Texans' defense has not been the dominant unit everyone expected so far in 2026, but they are still allowing the third-fewest rushing yards per game. They are also tied for 10th in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing running backs.

You can keep an eye out for Skattebo's snap count in this game as a potential indicator for how big his role in the offense might be going forward, but it's not worth giving him a starting spot until there's definitive proof he will be featured player for the Giants.

articles.title: In 2025, George Kittle signed a 4-year, $76.4 million 49ers contract extension that keeps him in San Francisco through 2029
articles.summary: George Kittle and the San Francisco 49ers agreed to a four-year, $76.4 million extension in April 2025, and it runs through 2029.
articles.body: George Kittle and the San Francisco 49ers agreed to a four-year, $76.4 million extension in April 2025, and it runs through 2029. The deal carries $40 million in guarantees and pays $19.1 million a year, the most of any tight end at that point. Kittle was 31 and one year from the end of his old contract. Then came a hamstring injury, a torn Achilles in January and a fast comeback this fall. Together, they show what the 49ers actually bought.What George Kittle's $76.4 million extension includesThe numbers are simple. Four years, $76.4 million, $19.1 million per year. Of the $40 million guaranteed, $35 million came at signing. That protects a little over half the money, which is solid but not the loudest figure on the market.George Kittle revealed the deal himself on the podcast Bussin' With The Boys, and ESPN's Adam Schefter confirmed it. "Third contract, same football team, great foundation, great organization," he said. It extended the five-year, $75 million deal he signed in 2020. It also ties him to San Francisco through his age-36 season.It wasn't a smooth negotiation. Reports in early April said the two sides were far apart. Kittle then skipped the first day of voluntary workouts, which some tied to the contract, though he denied that. A deal landed within weeks.Why the 49ers paid this much to a 31-year-old tight endStart with last season's production. Kittle caught 78 passes for 1,106 yards and eight touchdowns in 2024, his best yardage since 2018. He is a six-time Pro Bowler and was an All-Pro in 2019 and 2023. He also has more receiving yards than any tight end in team history.My read is that the numbers only tell half of it. Kittle blocks like a tackle and runs routes like a receiver, and that mix lets Kyle Shanahan call plays without tipping what is coming. You can't easily buy that on the open market. He was also a fifth-round pick in 2017, so the 49ers watched him grow from a skinny rookie into the face of the offense.General manager John Lynch had made the intent plain months earlier. "We want George to retire a Niner." The team had cut future cap costs in anticipation of paying both Kittle and quarterback Brock Purdy. Paying Kittle was planned, not a reaction.How the deal compares with Trey McBride'sKittle's crown was thinner than it looks. Arizona's Trey McBride signed a four-year, $76 million extension in early April 2025, with $43 million guaranteed and a $19 million average. Kittle passed that average by $100,000, about a month later.Look closer and McBride still wins one category. His guarantee is $3 million higher than Kittle's $40 million. That gap is the market pricing age. McBride was 25 and coming off a 111-catch season. Kittle was 31 and the team knew it, so the 49ers paid for the name and the past while protecting a little less of the future. Neither deal will hold the top spot for long, because younger tight ends keep arriving.Did the Achilles tear change the picture?It tested the deal sooner than anyone wanted. Kittle missed games early in 2025 with a leg injury. Then, in the Wild Card win over Philadelphia on January 11, 2026, he tore his right Achilles. He said it felt like "someone put a shotgun up against my calf."The recovery went better than expected. Kittle said the tear was high up near the soleus, which he called the best-case scenario. He called the rehab "the most boring rehab in the world." The 49ers activated him from the physically-unable-to-perform list in late August.He played under half the offensive snaps in the 27-7 opener against the Rams in Australia and had two catches on five targets. Ten days later he had four catches, 80 yards and a touchdown against Miami, and he reached 600 career catches. Only Jerry Rice and Kittle have done that in a 49ers uniform.The early returns are strong. Through four games he had 16 catches, 244 yards and four touchdowns. Shanahan joked, "I forgot about his Achilles." On a 56-yard score against Denver, Kittle hit 19.84 mph and outran former teammate Talanoa Hufanga.One month is not a verdict, and a 33-year-old tight end coming off Achilles surgery is a real risk. Still, the guarantee that looked generous in April 2025 now looks like a fair price for a player who beat the usual timeline. articles.title: Jim Nantz Talks Viral Video With JJ Watt, Says He Avoided Injury After 'Peanut Punch' Attempt
articles.summary: Jim Nantz's wrist is okay after his viral moment with JJ Watt during Sunday's broadcast of the Las Vegas Raiders vs. Buffalo Bills game when they were trying to demonstrate how to protect the ball.
articles.body:
Jim Nantz's wrist is okay after his viral moment with JJ Watt during Sunday's broadcast of the Las Vegas Raiders vs. Buffalo Bills game when they were trying to demonstrate how to protect the ball.

Appearing on Tuesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show , Nantz explained he got "a little too aggressive" with his punch but he will be "good to go" for his Week 7 assignment.

The situation occurred when Nantz and Watt were discussing the "Peanut Punch" and how players have adapted to protecting the ball to avoid having it knocked out.

Watt encouraged Nantz to try hitting the ball out of his hands by asking him to punch the ball as hard as he can, to which the legendary broadcaster obliged.

Watt seemed surprised Nantz hit the ball as hard as he did. Nantz said in the moment "my wrist is broken" and he had a wrap around his hand/wrist later in the game.

Nantz toughed it out for the remainder of the game, which turned out to be a thrilling offensive shootout won 33-30 by the Bills.

Watt joked on social media afterward that Nantz would be listed as questionable for Week 7. The 67-year-old is scheduled to be on the call for the Cincinnati Bengals-Baltimore Ravens matchup on Sunday.
